title.zh: 卷九十三 列傳第五十三 隱逸
title.raw: 卷九十三 列傳第五十三 隱逸 Volume 93 Biographies 53: Hermits

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十三 隱逸

translations.literal: Biographies 53: Hermits and Recluses
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 53: Hermits and Recluses

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天地閉，賢人隱。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "When heaven and earth are closed, the worthy withdraw into hiding."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "When heaven and earth are shut, the worthy withdraw from the world."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「遁世無悶。」

translations.literal: It also says: "To withdraw from the world without vexation."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Those who withdraw from the world have no cause for distress."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「高尚其事。」

translations.literal: It also says: "To hold one's affairs in high esteem."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "To hold one's own course in honor."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「幽人貞吉。」

translations.literal: It also says: "The secluded man is steadfast and fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The recluse who holds firm is blessed with good fortune."

sentences.zh: 《論語》「作者七人」，表以逸民之稱。

translations.literal: The Analects speaks of "seven authors," expressing the title of men who have withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects mentions "seven authors," a phrase that conveys the designation of withdrawn men.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「子路遇荷蓧丈人，孔子曰：隱者也。」

translations.literal: It also says: "When Zilu met the old man carrying a hoe, Confucius said: He is a recluse."
translations.idiomatic: It also says that when Zilu met the old man hoeing in the fields, Confucius remarked, "He is a recluse."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「賢者避地，其次避言。」

translations.literal: It also says: "The worthy avoid the land; the next best avoid speech."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The worthy withdraw from the realm; those of lesser rank withdraw from speech."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「虞仲，夷逸，隱居放言。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Yu Zhong and Yi Yi withdrew and lived in seclusion, speaking freely."
translations.idiomatic: It also says of Yu Zhong and Yi Yi that they withdrew from the world, lived in seclusion, and spoke without restraint.

sentences.zh: 品目參差，稱謂非一，請試言之：夫隱之為言，跡不外見，道不可知之謂也。

translations.literal: The categories are uneven and the designations not one; let me try to speak of them: as for the word "withdrawal," it means that one's traces do not appear outwardly and one's Way cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: The categories vary and the names are not uniform—let me attempt to explain. The word "withdrawal" denotes that one's traces do not appear in the world and one's Way cannot be discerned by others.

sentences.zh: 若夫千載寂寥，聖人不出，則大賢自晦，降夷凡品。

translations.literal: When a thousand years pass in silence and the sage does not appear, then the great worthy conceals himself and descends to the level of ordinary ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When ages pass in silence and no sage arises, the great worthy conceals his gifts and lowers himself to the level of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 止於全身遠害，非必穴處巖棲，雖藏往得二，鄰亞宗極，而舉世莫窺，萬物不睹。

translations.literal: He stops at preserving his person and keeping harm at a distance; he need not dwell in caves or nest on cliffs. Though he conceals what is past and attains the second [hexagram line], bordering on the ultimate of the lineage, yet the whole world cannot peer into him and the myriad things cannot behold him.
translations.idiomatic: His aim is simply to preserve his person and keep harm at bay—not necessarily to dwell in caves or perch on cliffs. Though he conceals his past attainments and stands near the highest rank, the whole world cannot see into him and the myriad things cannot perceive him.

sentences.zh: 若此人者，豈肯洗耳潁濱，皦皦然顯出俗之志乎！

translations.literal: Would such a person be willing to wash his ears at the banks of the Ying, brightly and clearly displaying his will to transcend the vulgar!
translations.idiomatic: Would such a man wash his ears at the Ying River, openly displaying his resolve to rise above the common world!

sentences.zh: 遁世避言，即賢人也。

translations.literal: To withdraw from the world and avoid speech—this is the worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: To withdraw from the world and refrain from speech—this describes the worthy man.

sentences.zh: 夫何適非世，而有避世之因，固知義惟晦道，非曰藏身。

translations.literal: Wherever he goes he is not of the age, yet he has the cause of avoiding the age; he surely knows that righteousness lies only in concealing the Way, not in hiding the body.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he goes he is out of step with the age, yet he has reason to withdraw from it; he knows that the point is to conceal the Way, not merely to hide one's person.

sentences.zh: 至於巢父之名，即是見稱之號，號曰裘公，由有可傳之跡。

translations.literal: As for the name of Chaofu, it is itself the designation by which he was praised; he was called Lord Qiu because there were traces that could be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: As for Chaofu, his very name was the title by which he was celebrated; he was called Lord Qiu because his deeds left traces that could be handed down.

sentences.zh: 此蓋荷蓧之隱，而非賢人之隱也。

translations.literal: This is the withdrawal of the hoe-carrier, not the withdrawal of the worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: This is the withdrawal of the man with the hoe, not the withdrawal of the worthy man.

sentences.zh: 賢人之隱，義深於自晦，荷蓧之隱，事止於違人。

translations.literal: The withdrawal of the worthy man lies deeper in self-concealment; the withdrawal of the hoe-carrier stops at defying others.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy man's withdrawal goes deeper—it is self-concealment in the fullest sense; the hoe-carrier's withdrawal goes no further than defying society.

sentences.zh: 論跡既殊，原心亦異也。

translations.literal: In discussing traces they are already different; in tracing the mind they are also distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Their outward traces differ, and the intentions behind them differ as well.

sentences.zh: 身與運閉，無可知之情，雞黍宿賓，示高世之美。

translations.literal: When body and fate are closed off, there is no sentiment that can be known; chicken and millet for an overnight guest show the beauty of transcending the age.
translations.idiomatic: When one's person and the times are shut off from each other, there is nothing others can know of one's inner state; offering chicken and millet to an overnight guest displays the beauty of rising above the world.

sentences.zh: 運閉故隱，為隱之跡不見；

translations.literal: Because the age is closed off, one withdraws, and the traces of withdrawal do not appear;
translations.idiomatic: Because the age is shut, one withdraws, and the traces of withdrawal remain unseen;

sentences.zh: 違人故隱，用致隱者之目。

translations.literal: because one defies others, one withdraws, and thereby incurs the label of "recluse."
translations.idiomatic: because one defies society, one withdraws, and thereby earns the name of "recluse."

sentences.zh: 身隱故稱隱者，道隱故曰賢人。

translations.literal: Because the body withdraws, one is called a recluse; because the Way withdraws, one is called a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: When the person withdraws, one is called a recluse; when the Way withdraws, one is called a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「隱者之異乎隱，既聞其說，賢者之同於賢，未知所異？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "We have heard the explanation of how recluses differ from withdrawal; as for how worthy men resemble the worthy, we do not yet know wherein they differ?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "We have heard how recluses differ from true withdrawal—but how do worthy men differ from one another when all are called worthy?"

sentences.zh: 應之曰：「隱身之於晦道，名同而義殊，賢人之於賢者，事窮於亞聖，以此為言，如或可辨。

translations.literal: The reply was: "Between concealing the body and concealing the Way, the names are the same but the meanings differ; between the worthy man and the worthy, affairs end at being next to the sage—speaking in these terms, perhaps it can be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The answer was: "Concealing the body and concealing the Way share a name but differ in meaning; among worthy men, the matter ends at standing next to the sage—in these terms, perhaps a distinction can be drawn.

sentences.zh: 若乃高尚之與作者，三避之與幽人，及逸民隱居，皆獨往之稱，雖復漢陰之氏不傳，河上之名不顯，莫不激貪厲俗，秉自異之姿，猶負揭日月，鳴建鼓而趨也。」

translations.literal: As for "holding affairs in honor" and "authors," the "three withdrawals" and "secluded men," and withdrawn subjects living in seclusion—all are designations of going one's own way. Though the clan of Han-yin left no transmission and the name of He-shang did not shine forth, none failed to stir the greedy and sharpen custom, bearing a posture of self-distinction, still shouldering the sun and moon, beating the war drum and rushing forward."
translations.idiomatic: Whether "holding one's course in honor," "authors," the "three withdrawals," "secluded men," or withdrawn subjects in retirement—all are titles for those who go their own way. Though the man of Han-yin left no record and the name of He-shang never shone forth, none failed to stir the greedy and sharpen custom, bearing an air of self-distinction—yet still they carried sun and moon on their backs, beat the war drum, and marched forward."

sentences.zh: 陳郡袁淑集古來無名高士，以為《真隱傳》，格以斯談，去真遠矣。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu of Chen commandery collected nameless eminent scholars of old and made the True Recluses Biography; measured by this discussion, it falls far from the true.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu of Chen commandery collected anonymous eminent scholars of antiquity into a True Recluses Biography; judged by this discussion, it falls far short of the genuine article.

sentences.zh: 賢人在世，事不可誣，今為《隱逸篇》，虛置賢隱之位，其餘夷心俗表者，蓋逸而非隱云。

translations.literal: Worthy men in the world—the matter cannot be falsified. Now in composing this chapter on Hermits and Recluses, we leave empty the place of the worthy recluse; the rest who level their hearts against the vulgar and set themselves apart are mostly withdrawn rather than hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men in the world cannot be misrepresented. In this chapter on Hermits and Recluses we leave the place of the truly hidden worthy vacant; those who level their hearts against vulgar custom and set themselves apart are for the most part withdrawn rather than truly hidden.

sentences.zh: 戴顒，字仲若，譙郡銍人也。

translations.literal: Dai Yong, style name Zhongruo, was a native of Qiao commandery, county of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yong, courtesy name Zhongruo, was a native of Cheng in Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父逵，兄勃，並隱遁有高名。

translations.literal: His father Kui and elder brother Bo both lived in withdrawal and had high renown.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui and elder brother Bo both lived in seclusion and enjoyed great renown.

sentences.zh: 顒年十六，遭父憂，幾於毀滅，因此長抱羸患。

translations.literal: At age sixteen Yong suffered his father's death and came near to ruining himself in grief; because of this he long carried a frail ailment.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Yong lost his father and nearly destroyed himself in mourning; from this he long suffered a frail constitution.

sentences.zh: 以父不仕，復脩其業。

translations.literal: Because his father did not take office, he again cultivated his father's pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had never entered office, he took up his father's pursuits once more.

sentences.zh: 父善琴書，顒並傳之，凡諸音律，皆能揮手。

translations.literal: His father was skilled at the zither and books; Yong received both traditions, and in all matters of pitch and rhythm he could perform with a wave of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: His father excelled at the zither and scholarship; Yong inherited both, and in every branch of music he could perform with ease.

sentences.zh: 會稽剡縣多名山，故世居剡下。

translations.literal: Shan county in Kuaiji had many famous mountains, so the family for generations dwelt below Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Shan county in Kuaiji boasted many famous mountains, and the family had long lived there.

sentences.zh: 顒及兄勃，並受琴於父。

translations.literal: Yong and his elder brother Bo both received the zither from their father.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and his elder brother Bo both learned the zither from their father.

sentences.zh: 父沒，所傳之聲，不忍復奏，各造新弄，勃五部，顒十五部。

translations.literal: After their father's death, they could not bear to play again the pieces he had transmitted; each composed new suites—Bo five suites, Yong fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: After their father died they could not bear to play his pieces again; each composed new suites—Bo five, Yong fifteen.

sentences.zh: 顒又制長弄一部，並傳於世。

translations.literal: Yong also composed one long suite, and both were transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yong also composed one long suite; both brothers' works were handed down to later generations.

sentences.zh: 中書令王綏常攜賓客造之，勃等方進豆粥，綏曰：「聞卿善琴，試欲一聽。」

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Sui often brought guests to visit them. Bo and the others were just taking bean porridge when Sui said: "I hear you are skilled at the zither; I would like to hear you play."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, Director of the Secretariat, often brought guests to visit them. Bo and the others were eating bean porridge when Sui said, "I hear you play the zither well—I should like to hear a piece."

sentences.zh: 不答，綏恨而去。

translations.literal: They did not answer; Sui left in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: They did not reply, and Sui left in resentment.

sentences.zh: 桐廬縣又多名山，兄弟復共游之，因留居止。

translations.literal: Tonglu county also had many famous mountains; the brothers again roamed them together and therefore remained to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Tonglu county also had many famous mountains; the brothers roamed them together and settled there.

sentences.zh: 勃疾患，醫藥不給。

translations.literal: Bo fell ill and medicine could not be provided.
translations.idiomatic: Bo fell ill, and they could not obtain adequate medical care.

sentences.zh: 顒謂勃曰：「顒隨兄得閒，非有心於默語。

translations.literal: Yong said to Bo: "Yong followed my brother to obtain leisure; I had no mind for silence and speech.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said to Bo, "I followed you into retirement for the leisure of it—I had no wish to embrace silence for its own sake.

sentences.zh: 兄今疾篤，無可營療，顒當幹祿以自濟耳。」

translations.literal: Now my brother's illness is grave and there is no way to arrange treatment; Yong must seek salary to support himself."
translations.idiomatic: Now your illness is grave and there is no way to pay for treatment—I must seek an official post to support us."

sentences.zh: 乃告時求海虞令，事垂行而勃卒，乃止。

translations.literal: He then petitioned the authorities to seek the post of magistrate of Haiyu; the matter was about to proceed when Bo died, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for the post of magistrate of Haiyu; the appointment was nearly settled when Bo died, and Yong abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 桐廬僻遠，難以養疾，乃出居吳下。

translations.literal: Tonglu was remote and far, difficult for nursing illness; he therefore went out to dwell in the Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: Tonglu was too remote to nurse an invalid, so he moved to the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 吳下士人共為築室，聚石引水，植林開澗，少時繁密，有若自然。

translations.literal: The gentlemen of the Wu region together built a dwelling for him, gathering stones and drawing water, planting groves and opening stream-beds; in a short time it grew dense, as if natural.
translations.idiomatic: Local scholars built a dwelling for him, piling stones, channeling water, planting groves and opening stream beds; in little time it grew lush, as though formed by nature itself.

sentences.zh: 乃述莊周大旨，著《逍遙論》，注《禮記·中庸》篇。

translations.literal: He then set forth the great purport of Zhuang Zhou, composed the Treatise on Free Wandering, and annotated the Doctrine of the Mean chapter of the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He then expounded the essential teachings of Zhuangzi, wrote the Treatise on Free and Easy Wandering, and annotated the Doctrine of the Mean in the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三吳將守及郡內衣冠要其同遊野澤，堪行便往，不為矯介，眾論以此多之。

translations.literal: The generals, guards, and gentry of the Three Wu regions who wished to roam the marshes with him—if travel was feasible he went; he was not artificially aloof, and public opinion for this reason praised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When generals, officials, and local gentry of the Three Wu invited him to roam the marshes, he went whenever travel was possible and made no show of aloofness; for this the public held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 高祖命為太尉行參軍，琅邪王司馬屬，並不就。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Acting Adjutant to the Grand Marshal and Attendant to the Prince of Langye's Secretariat; he accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Acting Adjutant to the Grand Marshal and Attendant in the Secretariat of the Prince of Langye; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，令曰：「前太尉參軍戴顒、辟士韋玄，秉操幽遁，守志不渝，宜加旌引，以弘止退。

translations.literal: When the Song state was first established, an edict said: "The former Adjutant to the Grand Marshal Dai Yong and the summoned gentleman Wei Xuan, holding to withdrawal in seclusion and keeping their resolve unchanging, should receive enhanced commendation to extend the principle of stopping and withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song state was first established, an edict declared: "The former Adjutant to the Grand Marshal Dai Yong and the summoned gentleman Wei Xuan, steadfast in secluded withdrawal, should receive special commendation to encourage others to follow their example of retirement.

sentences.zh: 並可散騎侍郎，在通直。」

translations.literal: Both may be Attendants of Scattered Cavalry, serving in the Office of Direct Access."
translations.idiomatic: Both are appointed Attendants of Scattered Cavalry in the Office of Direct Access."

sentences.zh: 不起。

translations.literal: He did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He did not accept.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉二年，詔曰：「新除通直散騎侍郎戴顒、太子舍人宗炳，並志托丘園，自求衡蓽，恬靜之操，久而不渝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia, Emperor Taizu issued an edict: "The newly appointed Attendant of Scattered Cavalry in Direct Access Dai Yong and the Household Attendant of the Heir Zong Bing both set their will in hill and garden, seeking thatched huts for themselves; their tranquil conduct has long been unchanging.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia, Emperor Taizu issued an edict: "The newly appointed Attendant of Scattered Cavalry in Direct Access Dai Yong and the Household Attendant of the Heir Zong Bing have both devoted themselves to life in hill and garden, choosing humble thatched dwellings; their tranquil conduct has long remained steadfast.

sentences.zh: 顒可國子博士，炳可通直散騎侍郎。」

translations.literal: Yong may be Erudite of the Imperial Academy; Bing may be Attendant of Scattered Cavalry in Direct Access."
translations.idiomatic: Yong is appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy; Bing is appointed Attendant of Scattered Cavalry in Direct Access."

sentences.zh: 東宮初建，又征太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was first established, he was again summoned as Household Vice-Intendant of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was first established, he was again summoned as Household Vice-Intendant of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 十五年，征散騎常侍，並不就。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; he accepted none of these posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was summoned as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季鎮京口，長史張邵與顒姻通，迎來止黃鵠山。

translations.literal: Prince Yiji of Hengyang was stationed at Jingkou; Chief Clerk Zhang Shao was connected to Yong by marriage and welcomed him to stay on Yellow Crane Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yiji of Hengyang was stationed at Jingkou, Chief Clerk Zhang Shao, who was related to Yong by marriage, invited him to stay on Yellow Crane Mountain.

sentences.zh: 山北有竹林精舍，林澗甚美。

translations.literal: North of the mountain was a bamboo-grove hermitage; the woods and streams were very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: North of the mountain stood a bamboo-grove hermitage amid woods and streams of rare beauty.

sentences.zh: 顒憩於此澗，義季亟從之遊，顒服其野服，不改常度。

translations.literal: Yong rested at this stream; Yiji frequently followed him on excursions. Yong wore his rustic garb and did not alter his usual manner.
translations.idiomatic: Yong made his retreat by this stream; Yiji often joined him on outings. Yong wore his rustic clothes and changed none of his usual ways.

sentences.zh: 為義季鼓琴，並新聲變曲，其三調《遊弦》、《廣陵》、《止息》之流，皆與世異。

translations.literal: He played the zither for Yiji, including new sounds and variant melodies; his three modes—"Wandering Strings," "Guangling," and "Ceasing Breath"—and the like were all unlike those of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He played the zither for Yiji, including new compositions and variant melodies; his versions of the three modes "Wandering Strings," "Guangling," and "Ceasing Breath" differed from those known in his day.

sentences.zh: 太祖每欲見之，嘗謂黃門侍郎張敷曰：「吾東巡之日，當晏戴公山也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu wished to see him on every occasion and once said to Attendant of the Yellow Gate Zhang Fu: "On the day of my eastern tour I shall feast with Lord Dai on the mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu often wished to see him and once told Attendant of the Yellow Gate Zhang Fu, "When I tour eastward, I shall feast with Lord Dai on his mountain."

sentences.zh: 以其好音，長給正聲伎一部。

translations.literal: Because he loved music, he was long provided with one company of orthodox-sound performers.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his love of music, the court long supplied him with a troupe of orthodox-sound performers.

sentences.zh: 顒合《何嘗》、《白鵠》二聲，以為一調，號為清曠。

translations.literal: Yong combined the two modes "He Chang" and "White Swan" into one mode, calling it Clear and Vast.
translations.idiomatic: Yong combined the two modes "He Chang" and "White Swan" into a single mode he called Clear and Vast.

sentences.zh: 自漢世始有佛像，形制未工，逵特善其事，顒亦參焉。

translations.literal: From the Han dynasty there began to be Buddha images, but the forms were not yet refined; Kui was especially skilled in this matter, and Yong also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha images had existed since the Han, but their forms were still crude; Kui was especially skilled in this art, and Yong assisted him.

sentences.zh: 宋世子鑄丈六銅像於瓦官寺，既成，面恨瘦，工人不能治，乃迎顒看之。

translations.literal: The Heir of Song cast a one-zhang-six Buddha image in bronze at Waguan Temple; when it was finished the face seemed regrettably thin and the craftsmen could not remedy it, so they welcomed Yong to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir of Song cast a sixteen-foot bronze Buddha at Waguan Temple; when it was finished the face seemed too thin and the craftsmen could not fix it, so they summoned Yong to examine it.

sentences.zh: 顒曰：「非面瘦，乃臂胛肥耳。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "It is not that the face is thin—it is that the arms and shoulders are too fat."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "The face is not too thin—the arms and shoulders are too heavy."

sentences.zh: 既錯減臂胛，瘦患即除，無不嘆服焉。

translations.literal: Once the arms and shoulders were reduced in error [i.e., corrected], the defect of thinness was at once removed, and none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Once the arms and shoulders were slimmed, the face looked right at once, and all marveled at his judgment.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died, at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he died, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 景陽山成，顒已亡矣。

translations.literal: When Jingyang Mountain was completed, Yong was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Jingyang Mountain was completed, Yong had already died.

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「恨不得使戴顒觀之。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed: "I regret that I could not have had Dai Yong view it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "How I regret that Dai Yong could not have seen it."

sentences.zh: 宗炳，字少文，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Zong Bing, style name Shaowen, was a native of Niyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Bing, courtesy name Shaowen, was a native of Niyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖承，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng served as Administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 父繇之，湘鄉令。

translations.literal: His father Youzhi was Magistrate of Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Youzhi was Magistrate of Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 母同郡師氏，聰辯有學義，教授諸子。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Shi clan of the same commandery, intelligent and eloquent with learning and righteousness, and she instructed her sons.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, née Shi of the same commandery, was intelligent, eloquent, and learned; she taught her sons herself.

sentences.zh: 炳居喪過禮，為鄉閭所稱。

translations.literal: Bing observed mourning beyond the rites and was praised by village and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Bing observed mourning with exceptional devotion and was praised throughout his community.

sentences.zh: 刺史殷仲堪、桓玄並辟主簿，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: Regional Inspectors Yin Zhongkan and Huan Xuan both summoned him as Chief Clerk and recommended him as Presented Scholar; he accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspectors Yin Zhongkan and Huan Xuan both summoned him as Chief Clerk and recommended him as Presented Scholar; he declined all appointments.

sentences.zh: 高祖誅劉毅，領荊州，問毅府諮議參軍申永曰：「今日何施而可？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu executed Liu Yi and took charge of Jing province, he asked Shen Yong, Consulting Adjutant in Yi's former staff: "What measures taken today would suffice?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu executed Liu Yi and took charge of Jing province, he asked Shen Yong, Consulting Adjutant on Yi's former staff, "What should be done today?"

sentences.zh: 永曰：「除其宿釁，倍其惠澤，貫敘門次，顯擢才能，如此而已。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "Remove their old grievances, double their gracious favors, arrange ranks in order, and prominently promote the capable—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied, "Clear away old grievances, redouble gracious treatment, set ranks in proper order, and promote the capable—that is all."

sentences.zh: 高祖納之，辟炳為主簿，不起。

translations.literal: Gaozu adopted this and summoned Bing as Chief Clerk; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu adopted this counsel and summoned Bing as Chief Clerk; he declined.

sentences.zh: 問其故，答曰：「棲丘飲谷，三十餘年。」

translations.literal: Asked the reason, he answered: "Dwelling on hills and drinking valley streams—for more than thirty years."
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he answered, "I have dwelt on hills and drunk from mountain streams for more than thirty years."

sentences.zh: 高祖善其對。

translations.literal: Gaozu approved of his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 妙善琴書，精於言理，每遊山水，往輒忘歸。

translations.literal: He was wonderfully skilled at the zither and books, refined in discourse on principle; whenever he roamed mountains and waters, on going he would forget to return.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at the zither and scholarship and was accomplished in philosophical discourse; whenever he roamed mountains and rivers he would lose track of time and forget to return.

sentences.zh: 征西長史王敬弘每從之，未嘗不彌日也。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Expeditionary West Wang Jinghong followed him on every occasion and never failed to spend the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinghong, Chief Clerk of the Expeditionary West, often accompanied him and never failed to spend the entire day together.

sentences.zh: 乃下入廬山，就釋慧遠考尋文義。

translations.literal: He then went down into Mount Lu and sought out the monk Huiyuan to examine and pursue textual meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Mount Lu and studied Buddhist doctrine under the monk Huiyuan.

sentences.zh: 兄臧為南平太守，逼與俱還，乃於江陵三湖立宅，閒居無事。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zang was Administrator of Nanping and compelled him to return together; he then established a dwelling at the Three Lakes of Jiangling and lived at leisure without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zang, Administrator of Nanping, compelled him to return home; he then built a house at the Three Lakes near Jiangling and lived in quiet retirement.

sentences.zh: 高祖召為太尉參軍，不就。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned him as Adjutant to the Grand Marshal; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned him as Adjutant to the Grand Marshal; he declined.

sentences.zh: 二兄蚤卒，孤累甚多，家貧無以相贍，頗營稼穡。

translations.literal: Two elder brothers died early; orphaned dependents were many and the family was poor with no means to support them, so he considerably engaged in farming.
translations.idiomatic: Two elder brothers had died young, leaving many dependents; the family was poor and could not support them all, so he took up farming.

sentences.zh: 高祖數致餼賚，其後子弟從祿，乃悉不復受。

translations.literal: Gaozu repeatedly sent gifts of food and bounty; afterward, when his younger kinsmen received salaries, he entirely ceased to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu repeatedly sent him gifts of food and goods; once his younger relatives began receiving official salaries, he refused all further gifts.

sentences.zh: 高祖開府辟召，下書曰：「吾忝大寵，思延賢彥，而《兔罝》潛處，《考槃》未臻，側席丘園，良增虛佇。

translations.literal: When Gaozu opened his headquarters and issued summons, he sent a document saying: "I am unworthy of great favor and think to extend invitation to worthy talents, yet the 'Rabbit Snares' lie hidden and the 'Kaopan' have not arrived; I lean from my seat toward hill and garden, truly increasing my empty waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu opened his headquarters and issued summons, he wrote: "Though unworthy of great favor, I wish to invite worthy men—yet like the hidden talents of the 'Rabbit Snares' ode and the recluse of the 'Kaopan,' they have not come; I lean from my seat toward hill and garden, and my longing only grows.

sentences.zh: 南陽宗炳、雁門周續之，並植操幽棲，無悶巾褐，可下辟召，以禮屈之。」

translations.literal: Zong Bing of Nanyang and Zhou Xuzhi of Yanmen both planted their conduct in secluded dwelling, without vexation in coarse cloth; summons may be sent down to bend them by ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Bing of Nanyang and Zhou Xuzhi of Yanmen both hold to secluded withdrawal in plain dress without regret; let summons be sent to bring them forth with due ceremony."

sentences.zh: 於是並辟太尉掾，皆不起。

translations.literal: Thereupon both were summoned as Attendants of the Grand Marshal; neither took office.
translations.idiomatic: Both were summoned as Attendants of the Grand Marshal; neither accepted.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，徵為太子舍人；

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication, he was summoned as Household Attendant of the Heir;
translations.idiomatic: When the Song received the mandate, he was summoned as Household Attendant of the Heir;

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，又征通直郎；

translations.literal: at the beginning of Yuanjia he was again summoned as Attendant in Direct Access;
translations.idiomatic: at the beginning of Yuanjia he was again summoned as Attendant in Direct Access;

sentences.zh: 東宮建，徵為太子中舍人，庶子，並不應。

translations.literal: when the Eastern Palace was established he was summoned as Household Scribe of the Heir and Household Tutor; he responded to none of these.
translations.idiomatic: when the Eastern Palace was established he was summoned as Household Scribe and Household Tutor of the Heir; he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 妻羅氏，亦有高情，與炳協趣。

translations.literal: His wife was of the Luo clan and also had lofty sentiment, sharing Bing's inclinations.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Luo, was also a person of lofty spirit and shared his tastes.

sentences.zh: 羅氏沒，炳哀之過甚，既而輟哭尋理，悲情頓釋。

translations.literal: When Lady Luo died, Bing grieved for her excessively; presently he ceased weeping and sought principle, and his sorrowful feeling was suddenly released.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Luo died, Bing grieved beyond measure; then he ceased weeping and turned to reason, and his sorrow lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 謂沙門釋慧堅曰：「死生不分，未易可達，三復至教，方能遣哀。」

translations.literal: He said to the monk Huijian: "Life and death are not divided—this is not easy to attain; only after thrice reviewing the ultimate teaching could I release my grief."
translations.idiomatic: He told the monk Huijian, "Life and death are not easily understood; only after thrice pondering the highest teaching could I release my grief."

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季在荊州，親至炳室，與之歡宴，命為諮議參軍，不起。

translations.literal: Prince Yiji of Hengyang was in Jing province; he came in person to Bing's dwelling, feasted merrily with him, and appointed him Consulting Adjutant; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiji of Hengyang, then in Jing province, visited Bing's home in person, feasted with him, and appointed him Consulting Adjutant; he declined.

sentences.zh: 好山水，愛遠遊，西陟荊、巫，南登衡、嶽，因而結宇衡山，欲懷尚平之志。

translations.literal: He loved mountains and waters and delighted in distant travel; he ascended west to Jing and Wu, climbed south to Heng and Yue, and therefore built a dwelling on Mount Heng, wishing to cherish the resolve of Shang Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape and distant travel; he climbed west to the Jing and Wu ranges and south to Heng and Yue, then built a house on Mount Heng in the spirit of the recluse Shang Ping.

sentences.zh: 有疾還江陵，歎曰：「老疾俱至，名山恐難遍睹，唯當澄懷觀道，臥以遊之。」

translations.literal: When illness came he returned to Jiangling and sighed: "Old age and illness have both arrived; famous mountains I fear will be hard to view in full—I can only clarify my heart and contemplate the Way, lying down to roam them."
translations.idiomatic: When illness overtook him he returned to Jiangling and sighed, "Old age and sickness have come together; I fear I shall never see all the famous mountains—I can only clear my mind, contemplate the Way, and roam them in my dreams."

sentences.zh: 凡所遊履，皆圖之於室，謂人曰：「撫琴動操，欲令眾山皆響。」

translations.literal: Every place he had roamed he painted on his chamber walls, saying to people: "When I stroke the zither and set the melody in motion, I wish to make all the mountains resound."
translations.idiomatic: Every place he had visited he painted on the walls of his room, telling others, "When I play the zither I mean to make all the mountains answer."

sentences.zh: 古有《金石弄》，為諸桓所重，桓氏亡，其聲遂絕，惟炳傳焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was the "Metal and Stone Suite," esteemed by the various Huans; when the Huan clan perished its sound was cut off, and only Bing transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there was the "Metal and Stone Suite," prized by the Huan clan; when the Huans fell its music was lost, and only Bing preserved it.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣樂師楊觀就炳受之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu sent the music master Yang Guan to Bing to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu sent the court musician Yang Guan to learn it from Bing.

sentences.zh: 炳外弟師覺授亦有素業，以琴書自娛。

translations.literal: Bing's cousin on his mother's side, Shi Jueshou, also had cultivated pursuits and amused himself with zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's maternal cousin Shi Jueshou was also accomplished in the arts and amused himself with the zither and books.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶辟為祭酒，主簿，並不就，乃表薦之，會病卒。

translations.literal: Prince Yiqing of Linchuan summoned him as Libationer and Chief Clerk; he accepted neither post. Yiqing then memorialized to recommend him, but Jueshou happened to die of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiqing of Linchuan summoned him as Libationer and Chief Clerk; he declined both. Yiqing then recommended him in a memorial, but Jueshou died of illness before the appointment could be made.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，炳卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia Bing died, at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia Bing died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季與司徒江夏王義恭書曰：「宗居士不救所病，其清履肥素，終始可嘉，為之惻愴，不能已已。」

translations.literal: Prince Yiji of Hengyang wrote to the Minister of Works, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia: "Layman Zong could not be saved from his illness; his pure conduct and simple abundance were admirable from first to last—I am deeply moved and cannot stop grieving."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiji of Hengyang wrote to the Minister of Works, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia: "Layman Zong could not be saved from his illness. His pure conduct and simple life were admirable from beginning to end; I am deeply grieved and cannot console myself."

sentences.zh: 子朔，南譙王義宣車騎參軍。

translations.literal: His son Shuo was Cavalry Adjutant to Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuo served as Cavalry Adjutant to Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 次綺，江夏王義恭司空主簿。

translations.literal: The next, Qi, was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Qi, was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 次昭，郢州治中。

translations.literal: The next, Zhao, was Administrator of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: The third son, Zhao, was Administrator of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 次說，正員郎。

translations.literal: The next, Yue, was Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son, Yue, was Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周續之，字道祖，雁門廣武人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuzhi, style name Daozu, was a native of Guangwu in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuzhi, courtesy name Daozu, was a native of Guangwu in Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 其先過江居豫章建昌縣。

translations.literal: His ancestors had crossed the river and dwelt in Jianchang county, Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had crossed the Yangzi and settled in Jianchang county, Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 續之年八歲喪母，哀戚過於成人，奉兄如事父。

translations.literal: At age eight Xuzhi lost his mother; his grief exceeded that of an adult, and he served his elder brother as he would a father.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhi lost his mother at eight; his grief surpassed that of a grown man, and he served his elder brother as he would a father.

sentences.zh: 豫章太守范寧於郡立學，招集生徒，遠方至者甚眾。

translations.literal: Administrator of Yuzhang Fan Ning established a school in the commandery and gathered students; those who came from afar were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ning, Administrator of Yuzhang, founded a school in the commandery and gathered students from far and wide.

sentences.zh: 續之年十二，詣寧受業。

translations.literal: At age twelve Xuzhi went to Ning to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve Xuzhi went to study under Fan Ning.

sentences.zh: 居學數年，通《五經》并《緯候》，名冠同門，號曰「顏子」。

translations.literal: After several years in study he mastered the Five Classics together with the Apocrypha and Prognostications, his name topping his fellow students; he was called "the Yanzi."
translations.idiomatic: After several years of study he mastered the Five Classics and the apocryphal texts, standing first among his peers; they called him "Little Yan."

sentences.zh: 既而閒居讀《老》、《易》，入廬山事沙門釋慧遠。

translations.literal: Presently he lived at leisure reading the Laozi and Changes, entered Mount Lu, and served the monk Huiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then retired to read the Laozi and the Book of Changes, went to Mount Lu, and studied under the monk Huiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時彭城劉遺民遁跡廬山，陶淵明亦不應徵命，謂之「尋陽三隱。」

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yimin of Pengcheng had hidden his traces on Mount Lu, and Tao Yuanming also did not respond to summons; they were called "the Three Recluses of Xunyang."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yimin of Pengcheng had withdrawn to Mount Lu, and Tao Yuanming also refused official summons; together with Xuzhi they were called "the Three Recluses of Xunyang."

sentences.zh: 以為身不可遣，餘累宜絕，遂終身不娶妻，布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: He held that the person could not be sent away and remaining encumbrances should be severed; he therefore never married in his lifetime and wore coarse cloth and ate plain food.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the body could not be cast off but worldly ties should be cut; he never married and lived on coarse cloth and plain food all his life.

sentences.zh: 劉毅鎮姑孰，命為撫軍參軍，征太學博士，並不就。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi was stationed at Gucuo he appointed Xuzhi Adjutant to the Pacification Army and summoned him as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; he accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi was stationed at Gucuo he appointed Xuzhi Adjutant to the Pacification Army and summoned him as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史每相招請，續之不尚節峻，頗從之遊。

translations.literal: The Regional Inspectors of Jiang province repeatedly invited him; Xuzhi did not esteem harsh austerity and quite often joined them on excursions.
translations.idiomatic: The Regional Inspectors of Jiang province often invited him; Xuzhi was not rigidly austere and often joined them on outings.

sentences.zh: 常以嵇康《高士傳》得出處之美，因為之注。

translations.literal: He often drew from Ji Kang's Biographies of Eminent Men the beauty of choosing office or withdrawal, and therefore annotated it.
translations.idiomatic: He often drew on Ji Kang's Biographies of Eminent Men for its wisdom on when to serve or withdraw, and wrote a commentary on it.

sentences.zh: 高祖之北討，世子居守，迎續之館於安樂寺，延入講禮，月餘，復還山。

translations.literal: When Gaozu marched north on campaign, the Heir remained to guard the capital and welcomed Xuzhi to lodge at Anle Temple, inviting him in to lecture on ritual; after more than a month he returned to the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched north, the Heir remained in the capital and lodged Xuzhi at Anle Temple, where he lectured on ritual for over a month before returning to the mountain.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史劉柳薦之高祖，曰：「臣聞恢耀和肆，必在兼城之寶；

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Jiang province Liu Liu recommended him to Gaozu, saying: "Your servant has heard that to extend brilliance and harmonize the marketplace, one must have the treasure of paired cities;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liu, Regional Inspector of Jiang province, recommended him to Gaozu, writing: "I have heard that to extend brilliance and harmonize the realm one must possess treasures of paired cities;

sentences.zh: 翼亮崇本，宜紆高世之逸。

translations.literal: to assist and illuminate what is fundamental, one should draw in the withdrawal of those who transcend the age.
translations.idiomatic: to assist and illuminate the fundamental order, one should draw in those lofty men who transcend the age.

sentences.zh: 是以渭濱佐周，聖德廣運，商洛匡漢，英業乃昌。

translations.literal: Therefore at the Wei banks one assisted Zhou and sagely virtue spread far; at Shang-luo one aided Han and heroic enterprise flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jiang Ziya at the Wei banks aided Zhou and sagely virtue spread wide; the Four Elders of Shangluo aided Han and heroic enterprise flourished.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明公道邁振古，應天繼期，游外暢於冥內，體遠形於應近，雖汾陽之舉，輟駕於時艱；

translations.literal: I bow to consider that Your Illustrious Lordship's Way surpasses the ancients and responds to Heaven in continuing the mandate; roaming outward you are expansive within the obscure, embodying the distant in what answers the near—though the raising at Fenyang paused its carriage in the hardship of the times;
translations.idiomatic: Your Illustrious Lordship's Way surpasses the ancients and answers Heaven's mandate; outwardly roaming yet inwardly profound, embodying the distant in what answers the near—though the raising at Fenyang paused in hard times;

sentences.zh: 明揚之旨，潛感於穹谷矣。

translations.literal: the intent to make the worthy illustrious has secretly moved the deep valleys.
translations.idiomatic: the intent to elevate the worthy has already stirred the deep valleys.

sentences.zh: 竊見處士雁門周續之，清真貞素，思學鉤深，弱冠獨往，心無近事，性之所遣；

translations.literal: I have observed the retired scholar Zhou Xuzhi of Yanmen—pure and true, chaste and plain, his thought and learning profound, in his weak-crowned years going his own way, his heart without near affairs, what his nature sends him forth to do;
translations.idiomatic: I have observed the retired scholar Zhou Xuzhi of Yanmen—pure and steadfast, his learning profound; since youth he has gone his own way, his heart free of worldly concerns, following only his nature;

sentences.zh: 榮華與饑寒俱落，情之所慕，巖澤與琴書共遠。

translations.literal: glory and splendor fall away together with hunger and cold; what his feeling admires—cliffs and marshes share distance with zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: glory and splendor mean nothing to him in hunger or cold; what he loves—cliffs and marshes, zither and books—are equally distant from the world.

sentences.zh: 加以仁心內發，義懷外亮，留愛昆卉，誠著桃李。

translations.literal: Moreover, benevolence arises within and righteousness shines outward; he leaves affection for all growing things, his sincerity manifest in peach and plum.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, benevolence wells within and righteousness shines without; he cherishes all living things, and his sincerity is known to all around him.

sentences.zh: 若升之宰府，必鼎味斯和；

translations.literal: If he were raised to the chief ministry, the flavors of the cauldron would surely harmonize;
translations.idiomatic: If raised to high office, the flavors of the state cauldron would harmonize;

sentences.zh: 濯纓儒官，亦王猷遐緝。

translations.literal: if he washed his tassel in the Confucian office, the king's plans would also be drawn far and gathered in.
translations.idiomatic: if he entered the Confucian service, the king's plans would reach far and succeed.

sentences.zh: 臧文不知，失在降賢；

translations.literal: Zang Wen did not know—his failure lay in demoting the worthy;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wen's failure lay in demoting the worthy;

sentences.zh: 言偃得人，功由升士。

translations.literal: Yan Yan obtained the right man—his achievement came from elevating scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yan's achievement came from elevating scholars.

sentences.zh: 願照其丹款，不以人廢言。」

translations.literal: I wish that his crimson sincerity be illumined, and that words not be rejected because of the man."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that you heed his sincere heart and do not reject his words because of the man who speaks them."

sentences.zh: 俄而辟為太尉掾，不就。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned as Attendant of the Grand Marshal; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was summoned as Attendant of the Grand Marshal; he declined.

sentences.zh: 王弘之，字方平，琅邪臨沂人，宣訓衛尉鎮之弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Hongzhi, style name Fangping, was a native of Linyi in Langye, younger brother of Zhenzhi, Commandant of the Guard for Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzhi, courtesy name Fangping, was a native of Linyi in Langye and younger brother of Zhenzhi, Commandant of the Guard for Instruction.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，為外祖徵士何准所撫育。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor and was reared by his maternal grandfather, the Summoned Scholar He Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he was raised by his maternal grandfather, the Summoned Scholar He Zhun.

sentences.zh: 從叔獻之及太原王恭，並貴重之。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Xianzhi and Wang Gong of Taiyuan both honored and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Xianzhi and Wang Gong of Taiyuan both held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安中，為琅邪王中軍參軍，遷司徒主簿。

translations.literal: In the Longan era of Emperor An of Jin he was Adjutant to the Central Army of the Prince of Langye, then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longan era of Emperor An of Jin he served as Adjutant to the Central Army of the Prince of Langye, then as Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 家貧，而性好山水，求為烏程令，尋以病歸。

translations.literal: His family was poor, but his nature loved mountains and waters; he sought the post of Magistrate of Wucheng and soon returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, he loved landscape; he sought the post of Magistrate of Wucheng but soon returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔晉，桓謙以為衛軍參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted Jin, Huan Qian appointed him Adjutant to the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan controlled the Jin court, Huan Qian appointed him Adjutant to the Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 時琅邪殷仲文還姑孰，祖送傾朝，謙要弘之同行，答曰：「凡祖離送別，必在有情，下官與殷風馬不接，無緣扈從。」

translations.literal: At that time Yin Zhongwen of Langye was returning to Gucuo; the whole court turned out to see him off. Qian wanted Hongzhi to go along and he answered: "Whenever one sees off a departing guest, there must be feeling between them. This inferior official and Yin are like wind and horse that do not meet—I have no cause to follow in attendance."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongwen of Langye returned to Gucuo, the whole court turned out to see him off. Qian asked Hongzhi to accompany him, but he replied, "A farewell requires genuine feeling between the parties. Yin and I have never been close—I have no reason to follow the procession."

sentences.zh: 謙貴其言。

translations.literal: Qian prized his words.
translations.idiomatic: Qian admired his reply.

sentences.zh: 每隨兄鎮之之安成郡，弘之解職同行，荊州刺史桓偉請為南蠻長史。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed his elder brother Zhenzhi to Ancheng commandery, Hongzhi resigned his post to travel with him. Regional Inspector of Jing province Huan Wei requested him as Chief Clerk of the Southern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his elder brother Zhenzhi went to Ancheng commandery, Hongzhi resigned his post to accompany him. Huan Wei, Regional Inspector of Jing province, invited him to serve as Chief Clerk of the Southern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 性好釣，上虞江有一處名三石頭，弘之常垂綸於此。

translations.literal: His nature loved angling; on the Shangyu River there was a place called Three Stones, and Hongzhi often let down his line there.
translations.idiomatic: He loved fishing; on the Shangyu River there was a spot called Three Stones where he often cast his line.

sentences.zh: 經過者不識之，或問：「漁師得魚賣不？」

translations.literal: Passersby did not recognize him; some asked: "Fisherman, do you get fish to sell?"
translations.idiomatic: Passersby did not recognize him; some asked, "Fisherman, do you sell your catch?"

sentences.zh: 弘之曰：「亦自不得，得亦不賣。」

translations.literal: Hongzhi said: "I often do not catch any; even when I catch fish I do not sell them."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I often catch nothing; and when I do, I do not sell them."

sentences.zh: 日夕載魚入上虞郭，經親故門，各以一兩頭置門內而去。

translations.literal: At dusk he would load fish into Shangyu town; passing the gates of kin and old friends, he would place one or two fish inside each gate and leave.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he carried his catch into Shangyu town and, passing the homes of kin and friends, left one or two fish inside each gate before moving on.

sentences.zh: 始寧汰川有佳山水，弘之又依巖築室。

translations.literal: The Taitai River in Shining had fine mountains and waters; Hongzhi again built a dwelling leaning on the cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: The Taitai River in Shining had fine scenery; Hongzhi built another dwelling against the cliffs there.

sentences.zh: 謝靈運、顏延之並相欽重，靈運與廬陵王義真箋曰：「會境既豐山水，是以江左嘉遁，並多居之。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun and Yan Yanzhi both honored and valued him. Lingyun wrote in a letter to Prince Yizhen of Luling: "The Kuaiji region is rich in mountains and waters, and therefore those who praised withdrawal in the Jiangzuo era mostly dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun and Yan Yanzhi both held him in high regard. Lingyun wrote to Prince Yizhen of Luling: "The Kuaiji region abounds in fine landscape, and many of the celebrated recluses of the Jiangzuo era made their homes there.

sentences.zh: 但季世慕榮，幽棲者寡，或復才為時求，弗獲從志。

translations.literal: But in a declining age men admire glory, and those who dwell in seclusion are few; some again are sought for their talent by the times and cannot follow their will.
translations.idiomatic: But in a declining age men chase glory, and true recluses are few; some are sought for their talent and cannot follow their own inclinations.

sentences.zh: 至若王弘之拂衣歸耕，踰歷三紀；

translations.literal: As for Wang Hongzhi, who shook off his robes and returned to farming—he has passed more than three twelve-year cycles;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzhi shook off his robes and returned to farming more than thirty-six years ago;

sentences.zh: 孔淳之隱約窮岫，自始迄今；

translations.literal: Kong Chunzhi has dwelt obscure in remote peaks from the beginning until now;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chunzhi has lived obscurely in remote mountains from the beginning until now;

sentences.zh: 阮萬齡辭事就閑，纂成先業；

translations.literal: Ruan Wanling resigned office and sought leisure, continuing and completing his forebears' enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Wanling resigned office for leisure and carried on his family's tradition;

sentences.zh: 浙河之外，棲遲山澤，如斯而已。

translations.literal: beyond the Zhe River, dwelling late in hills and marshes—only so many as these.
translations.idiomatic: beyond the Zhe River, dwelling in hills and marshes—only these few.

sentences.zh: 既遠同羲、唐，亦激貪厲競。

translations.literal: They are far from matching Fu Xi and Yao, yet they also stir the greedy and sharpen those who compete.
translations.idiomatic: Though they cannot match the sages of antiquity, they still stir the greedy and sharpen those who compete for gain.

sentences.zh: 殿下愛素好古，常若布衣，每憶昔聞，虛想巖穴，若遣一介，有以相存，真可謂千載盛美也。」

translations.literal: Your Highness loves simplicity and delights in antiquity, often like a commoner in cloth; whenever you recall what you have heard in the past, you vainly imagine cliff and cave—if you sent one messenger to keep them in mind, it would truly be called a splendor lasting a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness loves simplicity and antiquity and often dresses as a commoner; whenever you recall these men you yearn for their cliff-side lives—if you sent a messenger to visit them, it would be a glory to last a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 弘之四年卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Hongzhi died in the fourth year, at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi died in the fourth year, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 顏延之欲為作誄，書與弘之子曇生曰：「君家高世之節，有識歸重，豫染豪翰，所應載述。

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi wished to compose a dirge for him and wrote to Hongzhi's son Tansheng: "Your family's lofty conduct transcending the age—men of discernment turn to honor it; I have been touched by your noble brush and ought to record and narrate it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi wished to compose a dirge and wrote to Hongzhi's son Tansheng: "Your family's lofty conduct has won the respect of all discerning men; having been touched by your family's spirit, I ought to record it.

sentences.zh: 況僕托慕末風，竊以敘德為事，但恨短筆不足書美。」

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant trusts to admiration of the last breeze and privately takes narrating virtue as his task—but regrets that a short brush is insufficient to write the beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I who admire the last traces of your family's virtue take it as my task to record such excellence—but I fear my poor pen cannot do it justice."

sentences.zh: 誄竟不就。

translations.literal: The dirge in the end was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: The dirge was never completed.

sentences.zh: 曇生好文義，以謙和見稱。

translations.literal: Tansheng loved literary meaning and was praised for modesty and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Tansheng loved scholarship and was praised for his modesty and gentleness.

sentences.zh: 歷顯位，吏部尚書，太常卿。

translations.literal: He passed through eminent posts: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to eminent posts, including Minister of Personnel and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大明末，為吳興太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daming era he was Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daming era he served as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，四方同逆，戰敗奔會稽，歸降被宥，終於中散大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's reign, when the four quarters rebelled together, he was defeated in battle and fled to Kuaiji; on returning and submitting he was pardoned and ended as Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's reign, when rebellion broke out on all sides, he was defeated and fled to Kuaiji; on surrendering he was pardoned and ended his career as Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 阮萬齡，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Wanling was a native of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Wanling was a native of Weishi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 祖思曠，左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sikuan was Grand Master of Splendid Brightness on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sikuan served as Grand Master of Splendid Brightness on the Left.

sentences.zh: 父寧，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Ning was Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 萬齡少知名，自通直郎為孟昶建威長史。

translations.literal: Wanling was known from youth; from Attendant in Direct Access he became Chief Clerk of the Army Establishing Might under Meng Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wanling was known from youth; from Attendant in Direct Access he became Chief Clerk of the Army Establishing Might under Meng Chang.

sentences.zh: 時袁豹、江夷相係為昶司馬，時人謂昶府有三素望。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Bao and Jiang Yi succeeded one another as Chang's Secretariat Major; men of the time said Chang's staff had three men of plain repute.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bao and Jiang Yi served in succession as Chang's Secretariat Major; contemporaries said Chang's staff had three men of plain repute.

sentences.zh: 萬齡家在會稽剡縣，頗有素情。

translations.literal: Wanling's family was in Shan county, Kuaiji, and he had considerable plain sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Wanling's family was in Shan county, Kuaiji, and he cherished a simple, unworldly disposition.

sentences.zh: 永初末，自侍中解職東歸，徵為秘書監，加給事中，不就。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongchu he resigned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and returned east; he was summoned as Director of the Secretariat with additional appointment as Attendant, and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongchu he resigned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and returned east; summoned as Director of the Secretariat with additional appointment as Attendant, he declined.

sentences.zh: 尋除左民尚書，復起應命，遷太常，出為湘州刺史，在州無政績。

translations.literal: Shortly he was removed and made Minister of the Left for the People; he rose again and answered the summons, was transferred to Minister of Rites, went out as Regional Inspector of Xiang province, and in the province had no administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of the Left for the People, accepted the summons, rose to Minister of Rites, and went out as Regional Inspector of Xiang province, where he achieved nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 還為東陽太守，又被免。

translations.literal: On returning he became Administrator of Dongyang and was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he served as Administrator of Dongyang but was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 復為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He again became Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年卒，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he died, at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he died, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 孔淳之，字彥深，魯郡魯人也。

translations.literal: Kong Chunzhi, style name Yanshen, was a native of Lu in Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chunzhi, courtesy name Yanshen, was a native of Lu in Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites for Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan served as Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites for Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 父粲，秘書監徵，不就。

translations.literal: His father Can was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Can was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and declined.

sentences.zh: 淳之少有高尚，愛好墳籍，為太原王恭所稱。

translations.literal: Chunzhi from youth had lofty conduct, loved the classics and histories, and was praised by Wang Gong of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chunzhi was lofty in conduct, loved the classics, and was praised by Wang Gong of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 居會稽剡縣，性好山水，每有所遊，必窮其幽峻，或旬日忘歸。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Shan county, Kuaiji; his nature loved mountains and waters, and whenever he roamed he always exhausted their secluded steepness, sometimes forgetting to return for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Shan county, Kuaiji, loved landscape, and whenever he traveled explored every secluded peak, sometimes forgetting to return for ten days at a time.

sentences.zh: 當遊山，遇沙門釋法崇，因留共止，遂停三載。

translations.literal: Once when roaming the mountains he met the monk Fachong and therefore remained to lodge together, stopping for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Once while traveling in the mountains he met the monk Fachong and stayed with him for three years.

sentences.zh: 法崇歎曰：「緬想人外，三十年矣，今乃公傾蓋於茲，不覺老之將至也。」

translations.literal: Fachong sighed: "I have longed for life beyond the human world for thirty years; now at last we meet with overturned carriage-canopies here—I do not notice that old age is about to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Fachong sighed, "I have yearned for life beyond the human world for thirty years; now at last we meet as kindred spirits—I hardly notice that old age is upon me."

sentences.zh: 及淳之還反，不告以姓。

translations.literal: When Chunzhi returned he did not tell his surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunzhi left he did not reveal his surname.

sentences.zh: 除著作佐郎，太尉參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and Adjutant to the Grand Marshal; he accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and Adjutant to the Grand Marshal; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 居喪至孝，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: In mourning he was supremely filial and built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he was supremely filial and built a hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 服闋，與徵士戴顒、王弘之及王敬弘等共為人外之遊。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed he joined the Summoned Scholar Dai Yong, Wang Hongzhi, and Wang Jinghong in roaming beyond the human world.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he joined the Summoned Scholar Dai Yong, Wang Hongzhi, and Wang Jinghong in excursions beyond worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 敬弘以女適淳之子尚。

translations.literal: Jinghong gave his daughter in marriage to Chunzhi's son Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong gave his daughter in marriage to Chunzhi's son Shang.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守謝方明苦要入郡，終不肯往。

translations.literal: Administrator of Kuaiji Xie Fangming urgently pressed him to enter the commandery; he ultimately refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangming, Administrator of Kuaiji, urgently pressed him to enter the commandery; he steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 茅室蓬戶，庭草蕪徑，唯床上有數卷書。

translations.literal: His thatched chamber had a rush door; courtyard grass overgrew the path; on the bed alone were several scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a thatched hut with a rush door; grass overgrew the courtyard path; on his bed lay only a few scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，復徵為散騎侍郎，乃逃於上虞縣界，家人莫知所之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was again summoned as Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; he then fled to the border of Shangyu county and his family did not know where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was again summoned as Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; he fled to the border of Shangyu county, and his family did not know where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 弟默之為廣州刺史，出都與別。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mozhi was Regional Inspector of Guang province; leaving the capital he bade farewell.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mozhi, Regional Inspector of Guang province, came to the capital to bid him farewell before departing.

sentences.zh: 司徒王弘要淳之集冶城，即日命駕東歸，遂不顧也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Hong wanted Chunzhi to gather at Yecheng; that very day Chunzhi ordered his carriage and returned east, paying no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Hong invited Chunzhi to a gathering at Yecheng; that very day Chunzhi ordered his carriage eastward and paid no heed to the invitation.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he died, at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he died, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 默之儒學，注《谷梁春秋》。

translations.literal: Mozhi was learned in Confucian studies and annotated the Guliang Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhi was a Confucian scholar and wrote a commentary on the Guliang Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 默之子熙先，事在《范曄傳》。

translations.literal: Mozhi's son Xixian—his affairs are in the biography of Fan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhi's son Xixian is treated in the biography of Fan Ye.

sentences.zh: 劉凝之，字志安，小名長年，南郡枝江人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ningzhi, courtesy name Zhian, childhood name Changnian, was a native of Zhijiang in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ningzhi, styled Zhian and nicknamed Changnian, was a native of Zhijiang in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父期公，衡陽太守。

translations.literal: His father was Qi Gong, Governor of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi Gong served as Governor of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 兄盛公，高尚不仕。

translations.literal: His elder brother was Sheng Gong, lofty in character and refusing office.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Sheng Gong was a man of lofty character who refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 凝之慕老萊、嚴子陵為人，推家財與弟及兄子，立屋於野外，非其力不食，州裏重其德行。

translations.literal: Ningzhi admired the conduct of Old Master Lai and Yan Ziling; he gave away his family property to his younger brother and his brother's son, built a hut in the wilderness, and would not eat food not obtained by his own labor; the province and district held his virtue in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi admired the way Old Master Lai and Yan Ziling lived. He gave his family wealth to his younger brother and his brother's son, built a hut in the wild, and ate only what his own hands had earned. The province and district greatly respected his conduct.

sentences.zh: 州三禮辟西曹主簿，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: The province thrice sent formal invitations to appoint him Western Bureau Chief Clerk and recommended him as a Cultivated Talent; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Three times the province formally summoned him to serve as Western Bureau Chief Clerk and recommended him as a Cultivated Talent, but he declined every offer.

sentences.zh: 妻梁州刺史郭銓女也，遣送豐麗，凝之悉散之親屬。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Guo Quan, Regional Inspector of Liang province; when she was sent to him with rich and splendid goods, Ningzhi distributed them all among his relatives.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the daughter of Guo Quan, Regional Inspector of Liang province. When she arrived with lavish dowry goods, Ningzhi distributed everything among his kin.

sentences.zh: 妻亦能不慕榮華，與凝之共安儉苦。

translations.literal: His wife also was able not to covet glory and splendor, and together with Ningzhi she contentedly endured poverty and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: His wife likewise scorned rank and luxury, and together with Ningzhi she willingly endured a spare and hard life.

sentences.zh: 夫妻共乘薄笨車，出市買易，周用之外，輒以施人。

translations.literal: Husband and wife together rode a light clumsy cart, going to market to trade; whatever remained beyond their weekly needs, they always gave away to others.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife rode together in a simple rough cart to buy and sell at market; whatever they did not need for the week, they gave away to others.

sentences.zh: 為村里所誣，一年三輸公調，求輒與之。

translations.literal: He was falsely accused by the village; three times in one year he was assessed for official levies, and whenever they came seeking payment he always gave it to them.
translations.idiomatic: The village falsely implicated him in tax obligations; three times in a single year he was charged official levies, and each time they came to collect, he paid without dispute.

sentences.zh: 有人嘗認其所著屐，笑曰：「僕著之已敗，今家中覓新者備君也。」

translations.literal: Someone once claimed the sandals he was wearing; he laughed and said: "I have worn these until they are worn out; I will find new ones at home for you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Once someone claimed the sandals on his feet. He laughed and said, "I've worn these until they're ruined—I'll find new ones at home for you, sir."

sentences.zh: 此人後田中得所失屐，送還之，不肯復取。

translations.literal: Later this man found his lost sandals in the fields and returned them, but Ningzhi refused to take them back.
translations.idiomatic: Later the man recovered his lost sandals from the fields and brought them back, but Ningzhi would not accept them.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，徵為秘書郎，不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, he was summoned as Secretary Gentleman; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanjia era, he was summoned to serve as Secretary Gentleman but declined.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶、衡陽王義季鎮江陵，並遣使存問。

translations.literal: Prince Linchuan Yi Qing and Prince Hengyang Yi Ji were stationed at Jiangling and both sent messengers to inquire after his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Linchuan Yi Qing and Prince Hengyang Yi Ji were both stationed at Jiangling and sent messengers to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 凝之答書頓首稱僕，不脩民禮，人或譏焉。

translations.literal: Ningzhi's reply letter used "your servant" with a bow; he did not observe the rites due to commoners, and some people ridiculed this.
translations.idiomatic: In his reply Ningzhi bowed and addressed himself as "your servant," omitting the usual courtesies owed to men of rank, and some people mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 凝之曰：「昔老萊向楚王稱僕，嚴陵亦抗禮光武，未聞巢、許稱臣堯、舜。」

translations.literal: Ningzhi said: "In the past Old Master Lai called himself 'your servant' to the King of Chu, and Yan Ziling also treated Emperor Guangwu as an equal in ritual; one never heard that Chao and Xu called themselves subjects to Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi said, "Long ago Old Master Lai addressed the King of Chu as 'your servant,' and Yan Ziling likewise treated Emperor Guangwu as an equal in ritual. No one ever said that Chao and Xu styled themselves subjects of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 時戴顒與衡陽王義季書，亦稱僕。

translations.literal: At that time Dai Yong in his letter to Prince Hengyang Yi Ji also used "your servant."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dai Yong, writing to Prince Hengyang Yi Ji, also addressed himself as "your servant."

sentences.zh: 荊州年饑，義季慮凝之餧斃，餉錢十萬。

translations.literal: Jing province suffered famine that year; Yi Ji worried Ningzhi would starve to death and sent him one hundred thousand coins in relief.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jing province suffered famine. Yi Ji feared Ningzhi might starve and sent him one hundred thousand coins in relief.

sentences.zh: 凝之大喜，將錢至市門，觀有饑色者，悉分與之，俄頃立盡。

translations.literal: Ningzhi was greatly pleased; he took the money to the market gate, and seeing those with hungry faces, he distributed it all to them, and in no time it was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi was delighted. He took the money to the market gate, and seeing people with hungry faces, he gave it all away; in moments it was spent.

sentences.zh: 性好山水，一旦攜妻子泛江湖，隱居衡山之陽。

translations.literal: His nature loved mountains and rivers; one day he took his wife and children and sailed the rivers and lakes, and went into seclusion on the southern slope of Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: He loved mountains and rivers by nature. One day he took wife and children and sailed the rivers and lakes, settling in seclusion on the southern slope of Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 登高嶺，絕人跡，為小屋居之，采藥服食，妻子皆從其志。

translations.literal: He climbed high peaks where no human tracks reached, built a small hut to dwell in, gathered herbs and consumed them for nourishment; wife and children all followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to high ridges where no footfall reached, built a small hut, and gathered herbs for nourishment. His wife and children all followed his wish.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年，卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 龔祈，字孟道，武陵漢壽人也。

translations.literal: Gong Qi, courtesy name Mengdao, was a native of Hanshou in Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Qi, styled Mengdao, was a native of Hanshou in Wuling.

sentences.zh: 從祖玄之，父黎民，並不應徵辟。

translations.literal: His great-uncle was Xuanzhi; his father Limin—both did not respond to summoning invitations.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle Xuanzhi and his father Limin both refused every summons to office.

sentences.zh: 祈年十四，鄉黨舉為州迎西曹，不行。

translations.literal: At fourteen Qi was recommended by his village and district as the province's welcoming Western Bureau officer; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen the local community recommended him as the province's welcoming Western Bureau officer, but he would not go.

sentences.zh: 謝晦臨州，命為主簿；

translations.literal: When Xie Hui came to the province he appointed Qi as Chief Clerk;
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui arrived to govern the province, he appointed Qi Chief Clerk;

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康舉秀才，除奉朝請；

translations.literal: Prince Pengcheng Yi Kang recommended him as Cultivated Talent and appointed him Attendant at Court;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng Yi Kang recommended him as Cultivated Talent and appointed him Attendant at Court;

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶平西參軍，皆不就。

translations.literal: Prince Linchuan Yi Qing [appointed him] Western Pacification Army Adjutant—all of which he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Linchuan Yi Qing appointed him Western Pacification Army Adjutant—all of which he declined.

sentences.zh: 風姿端雅，容止可觀，中書郎范述見而歎曰：「此荊楚仙人也。」

translations.literal: His bearing was dignified and elegant, his deportment worthy of regard; Attendant Director Fan Shu saw him and sighed: "This is an immortal of Jing-Chu."
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was dignified and elegant, his deportment admirable. Attendant Director Fan Shu saw him and sighed, "This is an immortal of Jing and Chu."

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季臨荊州，發教以祈及劉凝之、師覺授不應徵召，辟其三子。

translations.literal: Prince Hengyang Yi Ji came to Jing province and issued an instruction that because Qi, Liu Ningzhi, and Shi Jueshou did not respond to recruitment summons, [the prince] recruited their three sons instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hengyang Yi Ji came to govern Jing province, he issued an instruction that because Qi, Liu Ningzhi, and Shi Jueshou would not answer summons, he would recruit their three sons instead.

sentences.zh: 祈又徵太子舍人，不起。

translations.literal: Qi was again summoned as Retainer of the Heir Apparent; he did not rise [to take office].
translations.idiomatic: Qi was again summoned as Retainer of the Heir Apparent but did not accept.

sentences.zh: 時或賦詩，言不及世事。

translations.literal: Occasionally he composed poems, and their words never touched on affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes wrote poetry, but his words never touched on the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十七年，卒，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia he died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of Yuanjia, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 翟法賜，尋陽柴桑人也。

translations.literal: Zhai Fasi was a native of Chaisang in Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Fasi was a native of Chaisang in Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖湯，湯子莊，莊子矯，並高尚不仕，逃避徵辟。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Tang; Tang's son Zhuang; Zhuang's son Jiao—all lofty and refusing office, evading summoning invitations.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tang, Tang's son Zhuang, and Zhuang's son Jiao were all men of lofty character who refused office and evaded every summons.

sentences.zh: 矯生法賜。

translations.literal: Jiao fathered Fasi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was Fasi's father.

sentences.zh: 少守家業，立屋於廬山頂，喪親後，便不復還家。

translations.literal: In youth he maintained the family estate and built a hut on the summit of Mount Lu; after his parents' death he never returned home again.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he kept the family estate and built a hut on the summit of Mount Lu. After his parents died, he never returned home.

sentences.zh: 不食五穀，以獸皮結草為衣，雖鄉親中表，莫得見也。

translations.literal: He did not eat grain; he made clothing from animal hides plaited with grass; even among village kin and cousins, none could see him.
translations.idiomatic: He ate no grain and wore clothes woven from animal hides and grass. Even kin and cousins in the village could not see him.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，右參軍，著作佐郎，員外散騎侍郎，並不就。

translations.literal: The province appointed him Chief Clerk, recommended him as Cultivated Talent, Right Army Adjutant, Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section, and Supernumerary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry—all of which he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province appointed him Chief Clerk, recommended him as Cultivated Talent, and offered him posts as Right Army Adjutant, Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section, and Supernumerary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry—all of which he declined.

sentences.zh: 後家人至石室尋求，因復遠徙，違避徵聘，遁跡幽深。

translations.literal: Later when his family came seeking him in the stone chamber, he moved far away again, evading recruitment and summons, his traces hidden in the deepest seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his family came to seek him in his stone chamber, he moved farther away again, evading recruitment and summons and hiding his tracks in the deepest wilds.

sentences.zh: 尋陽太守鄧文子表曰：「奉詔書徵郡民新除著作佐郎南陽翟法賜，補員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Prefect of Xunyang Deng Wenzi submitted a memorial saying: "In accord with the imperial decree we summon the county subject newly appointed Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section, Zhai Fasi of Nanyang, to fill the post of Supernumerary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
