translations.idiomatic: Deng Wenzi, Prefect of Xunyang, submitted a memorial saying, "By imperial decree we summon the county subject Zhai Fasi of Nanyang, newly appointed Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section, to fill the post of Supernumerary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 法賜隱跡廬山，於今四世，棲身幽巖，人罕見者。

translations.literal: Fasi has lived in seclusion on Mount Lu, now for four generations, dwelling in deep cliffs—a man rarely seen by others.
translations.idiomatic: Fasi has lived in seclusion on Mount Lu for four generations now, dwelling in deep cliffs—a man scarcely ever seen.

sentences.zh: 如當逼以王憲，束以嚴科，馳山獵草，以期禽獲，慮致顛殞，有傷盛化。」

translations.literal: If we should compel him with royal ordinances, bind him with strict law, sweep the mountains and hunt through the grasslands expecting to capture him like game, I fear it would cause his fall and death and wound the flourishing virtue [of the age]."
translations.idiomatic: If we should force him with royal ordinances and bind him with harsh law, sweep the mountains and hunt the grasslands expecting to capture him like game, I fear he would come to ruin and the age's flourishing virtue would be harmed."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: [The court] thereupon stopped [the pursuit].
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 後卒於巖石之間，不知年月。

translations.literal: Later he died among the cliffs and rocks; the year and month are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He later died among the cliffs and rocks; the year and month are unknown.

sentences.zh: 陶潛，字淵明，或云淵明，字元亮，尋陽柴桑人也，曾祖侃，晉大司馬。

translations.literal: Tao Qian, courtesy name Yuanming (some say his given name was Yuanming and courtesy name Yuanliang), was a native of Chaisang in Xunyang; his great-grandfather Kan was Grand Commander of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian, styled Yuanming—though some say his given name was Yuanming and his style Yuanliang—was a native of Chaisang in Xunyang. His great-grandfather Kan was Grand Commander of Jin.

sentences.zh: 潛少有高趣，嘗著《五柳先生傳》以自況，曰：

translations.literal: Qian from youth had lofty inclinations; he once wrote "Biography of Mr. Five Willows" to describe himself, saying:
translations.idiomatic: From youth Qian had lofty tastes. He once wrote "Biography of Mr. Five Willows" to describe himself, saying:

sentences.zh: 先生不知何許人，不詳姓字，宅邊有五柳樹，因以為號焉。

translations.literal: The gentleman does not know from what place he comes; his surname and given name are not recorded. By his dwelling were five willow trees, and on that account he took it as his byname.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman does not know from what place he comes, and his surname and given name are not recorded. Five willow trees stood by his dwelling, and on that account he took them as his byname.

sentences.zh: 閒靜少言，不慕榮利。

translations.literal: Quiet and retiring, sparing of speech; he did not covet glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and retiring, sparing of speech, he did not covet rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，不求甚解，每有會意，欣然忘食。

translations.literal: He loved to read books, without seeking deep understanding; whenever he grasped the meaning, he was delighted and forgot to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to read but did not pursue exhaustive understanding; whenever he grasped a passage's meaning, he was so pleased he forgot to eat.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，而家貧不能恆得。

translations.literal: By nature he was fond of wine, yet his family was poor and could not always obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved wine, but his family was poor and could not always keep it on hand.

sentences.zh: 親舊知其如此，或置酒招之。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends knowing this, sometimes set out wine to invite him.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends, knowing this, sometimes set out wine to invite him over.

sentences.zh: 造飲輒盡，期在必醉，既醉而退，曾不吝情去留。

translations.literal: When he went drinking he always drained the cup; his intent was necessarily to become drunk; once drunk he withdrew, never stinting feeling in coming or going.
translations.idiomatic: When he drank, he always emptied the cup, intent on getting thoroughly drunk. Once drunk he would leave, never troubling himself over comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 環堵蕭然，不蔽風日，短褐穿結，簞瓢屢空，晏如也。

translations.literal: Four bare walls, desolate; they barely sheltered from wind and sun; short hempen coat, patched and tied; bamboo basket and gourd often empty—yet he was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: His four walls were bare and desolate, barely keeping out wind and sun; his short hemp coat was patched and tied; his bamboo basket and gourd were often empty—yet he was content.

sentences.zh: 嘗著文章自娛，頗示己志，忘懷得失，以此自終。

translations.literal: He sometimes wrote essays to amuse himself, showing clearly his intent; forgetting gain and loss, with this he ended his days.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes wrote essays to amuse himself, making his intent plain, and forgetting gain and loss lived out his days in this way.

sentences.zh: 其自序如此，時人謂之實錄。

translations.literal: His self-account was such; men of the time called it a true record.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his self-portrait; men of the time called it a faithful account.

sentences.zh: 親老家貧，起為州祭酒，不堪吏職，少日，自解歸。

translations.literal: His parents were aged and his family poor; he took office as Libationer of the province but could not bear the duties of a clerk; in a few days he resigned of his own accord and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: His parents were old and his family poor, so he took office as Libationer of the province, but he could not endure the duties of an official. Within a few days he resigned on his own and returned home.

sentences.zh: 州召主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Chief Clerk; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province summoned him to serve as Chief Clerk, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 躬耕自資，遂抱羸疾，復為鎮軍、建威參軍。

translations.literal: He plowed the fields to support himself, then contracted a wasting illness; he again took office as Adjutant to the General of Pacification and the General Establishing Might.
translations.idiomatic: He plowed to support himself, then fell ill with a wasting sickness and again took office as adjutant to the Generals of Pacification and Establishing Might.

sentences.zh: 謂親朋曰：「聊欲弦歌，以為三徑之資，可乎？」

translations.literal: He said to relatives and friends: "For the moment I wish to play the zither and sing, to provide for the three paths—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: He told relatives and friends, "For now I mean to play the zither and sing, to earn a living for my three paths—is that all right?"

sentences.zh: 執事者聞之，以為彭澤令。

translations.literal: Those in charge heard this and made him magistrate of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge heard this and appointed him magistrate of Pengze.

sentences.zh: 公田悉令吏種秫稻。

translations.literal: The public fields—all he ordered the clerks to plant glutinous millet.
translations.idiomatic: Of the public fields, he ordered the clerks to plant every acre in glutinous millet.

sentences.zh: 妻子固請種粳，乃使二頃五十畝種秫，五十畝種粳。

translations.literal: Wife and children firmly requested planting non-glutinous rice; he therefore had two qing and fifty mu planted with glutinous millet, and fifty mu with non-glutinous rice.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children insisted on planting non-glutinous rice, so in the end he had two qing and fifty mu sown with glutinous millet and fifty mu with non-glutinous rice.

sentences.zh: 郡遣督郵至，縣吏白應束帶見之。

translations.literal: The prefecture sent the Inspector to arrive; the county clerks reported he should gird himself and go see him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture sent an Inspector; the county clerks reported that he should gird himself formally and go to receive him.

sentences.zh: 潛歎曰：「我不能為五斗米折腰向鄉里小人。」

translations.literal: Qian sighed and said: "I cannot bow my waist for five pecks of rice before the petty men of the village."
translations.idiomatic: Qian sighed and said, "I cannot bow my waist for five pecks of rice before the petty men of the village."

sentences.zh: 即日解印綬去職。

translations.literal: That same day he resigned his seal and ribbon and left office.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he resigned his seal and ribbon and left office.

sentences.zh: 賦《歸去來》，其詞曰：

translations.literal: He composed "Returning Home"; the words say:
translations.idiomatic: He composed "Returning Home"; its words say:

sentences.zh: 歸去來兮，園田荒蕪胡不歸。

translations.literal: Returning home—oh, my garden and fields lie waste and overgrown; why do I not return?
translations.idiomatic: Home I go! My garden and fields lie waste and overgrown—why do I not return?

sentences.zh: 既自以心為形役，奚惆悵而獨悲。

translations.literal: Having let my heart be slave to my form, why grieve and sorrow alone?
translations.idiomatic: Having let my heart be slave to my body, why brood and grieve alone?

sentences.zh: 悟已往之不諫，知來者之可追。

translations.literal: I understand that what is past cannot be admonished, yet know that what is to come may still be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: I see that the past cannot be undone, yet know that what lies ahead may still be reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 實迷途其未遠，覺今是而昨非。

translations.literal: Truly I had strayed but not far; I awake to today's right and yesterday's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I had strayed, but not far; I awake to today's right and yesterday's wrong.

sentences.zh: 舟遙遙以輕颺，風飄飄而吹衣。

translations.literal: The boat sways far off, lightly riding the breeze; the wind flutters, blowing my robe.
translations.idiomatic: My boat sways far off, lightly riding the breeze; the wind flutters, blowing my robe.

sentences.zh: 問征夫以前路，恨晨光之希微。

translations.literal: I ask the traveler about the road ahead, and regret the dawn light is so faint.
translations.idiomatic: I ask the wayfarer about the road ahead and regret how faint the dawn light is.

sentences.zh: 乃瞻衡宇，載欣載奔。

translations.literal: Then I behold my humble house and run with joy mixed with delight.
translations.idiomatic: Then I catch sight of my humble house and run with mingled joy and exultation.

sentences.zh: 僮僕歡迎，稚子候門。

translations.literal: Servants welcome me; my young child waits at the door.
translations.idiomatic: Servants welcome me; my young child waits at the door.

sentences.zh: 三徑就荒，松菊猶存。

translations.literal: The three paths are nearly overgrown, but pine and chrysanthemum remain.
translations.idiomatic: The three paths are nearly overgrown, but pine and chrysanthemum still stand.

sentences.zh: 攜幼入室，有酒停尊。

translations.literal: Taking the little ones into the inner room, there is wine resting in the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the little ones into the inner room, I find wine resting in the goblet.

sentences.zh: 引壺觴而自酌，盼庭柯以怡顏。

translations.literal: I draw the wine cup and pour for myself, gazing at the courtyard branches to please my face.
translations.idiomatic: I draw the wine cup and pour for myself, gazing at the courtyard branches until pleasure shows on my face.

sentences.zh: 倚南窗而寄傲，審容膝之易安。

translations.literal: Leaning on the south window I lodge my pride; I see that a space to fit the knees is easily at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on the south window I lodge my ease; I see that a space to fit the knees is easily enough.

sentences.zh: 園日涉而成趣，門雖設而常關。

translations.literal: Daily I stroll the garden and it becomes delight; though the gate is set up, it is often closed.
translations.idiomatic: Daily I stroll the garden and it becomes my delight; though the gate is there, it stays often closed.

sentences.zh: 策扶老以流悽，時矯首而遐觀，雲無心以出岫，鳥倦飛而知還。

translations.literal: Leaning on my cane I wander at leisure; from time to time I raise my head for a distant view—clouds without intent drift from the mountain fold; birds weary of flight know to return.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on my cane I wander at leisure; now and then I raise my head for a distant view—clouds without intent drift from the mountain fold; birds weary of flight know to return.

sentences.zh: 景翳翳其將入，撫孤松以盤桓。

translations.literal: The sun's glow dims as it is about to set; I stroke the solitary pine and linger.
translations.idiomatic: The light dims as the sun is about to set; I stroke the solitary pine and linger.

sentences.zh: 歸去來兮，請息交而絕遊，世與我以相遺，復駕言兮焉求。

translations.literal: Returning home—oh, please cease mingling and cut off wanderings; the world and I have cast each other off; why drive my carriage forth—what would I seek?
translations.idiomatic: Home I go! Let me cease mingling and cut off wanderings—the world and I have cast each other off; why drive my carriage forth, and what would I seek?

sentences.zh: 說親戚之情話，樂琴書以消憂。

translations.literal: I speak of kinship with relatives and delight in the zither and books to dispel sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: I speak with kin of family matters and take joy in zither and books to dispel sorrow.

sentences.zh: 農人告餘以上春，將有事於西疇。

translations.literal: The farmer tells me spring is advanced and that there will be work in the western field.
translations.idiomatic: The farmer tells me spring is well advanced and that there will be work in the western field.

sentences.zh: 或命巾車，或棹扁舟。

translations.literal: Sometimes I command a covered cart; sometimes I pole a flat boat.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes I call for a covered cart; sometimes I pole a flat boat.

sentences.zh: 既窈窕以窮壑，亦崎嶇而經丘。

translations.literal: Now through winding depths to the end of ravines, now over rugged paths across hillocks.
translations.idiomatic: Now through winding depths to the end of ravines, now over rugged paths across hillocks.

sentences.zh: 木欣欣以向榮，泉涓涓而始流。

translations.literal: Trees flourish and turn toward glory; springs trickle and begin to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Trees flourish and turn toward glory; springs trickle and begin to flow.

sentences.zh: 善萬物之得時，感吾生之行休。

translations.literal: I rejoice that the myriad things receive their season; I feel that my life's journey is nearing its end.
translations.idiomatic: I rejoice that the myriad things receive their season; I feel that my life's journey is nearing its end.

sentences.zh: 已矣乎，寓形宇內復幾時，奚不委心任去留，胡為遑遑欲何之。

translations.literal: Enough! How much longer shall this form lodge within the universe? Why not entrust the heart and leave coming and going to fate—why hasten anxiously, whither would I go?
translations.idiomatic: Enough! How long will this form lodge within the universe? Why not entrust the heart and leave coming and going to fate—why hurry anxiously, and whither would I go?

sentences.zh: 富貴非吾願，帝鄉不可期。

translations.literal: Wealth and honor are not my wish; the imperial domain cannot be counted on.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and honor are not my wish; the imperial domain is not to be counted on.

sentences.zh: 懷良辰以孤往，或植杖而耘耔。

translations.literal: On fine days I go alone, or lean on my staff and weed the seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: On fine days I go alone, or lean on my staff and weed the seedlings.

sentences.zh: 登東皋以舒嘯，臨清流而賦詩。

translations.literal: I climb the eastern terrace and release a long whistle; beside clear currents I compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: I climb the eastern terrace and release a long whistle; beside clear streams I compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 聊乘化以歸盡，樂夫天命復奚疑。

translations.literal: For a time I ride transformation and return to the end; I rejoice in Heaven's decree—what more is there to doubt?
translations.idiomatic: For a time I ride transformation and return to the end; I rejoice in Heaven's decree—what more is there to doubt?

sentences.zh: 義熙末，徵著作佐郎，不就。

translations.literal: At the end of Yixi, he was summoned as Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yixi era he was summoned as Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section but declined.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史王弘欲識之，不能致也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, Regional Inspector of Jiang province, wished to know him but could not arrange a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, Regional Inspector of Jiang province, wished to meet him but could not arrange it.

sentences.zh: 潛嘗往廬山，弘令潛故人龐通之齎酒具於半道栗里要之。

translations.literal: Qian once went to Mount Lu; Hong had Qian's old friend Pang Tongzhi carry wine and vessels to intercept him halfway at Lili.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Qian was going to Mount Lu, Hong had his old friend Pang Tongzhi carry wine and vessels to meet him halfway at Lili.

sentences.zh: 潛有腳疾，使一門生二兒輿籃輿，既至，欣然便共飲酌，俄頃弘至，亦無忤也。

translations.literal: Qian had a foot ailment; he had one student and two sons carry a basket sedan; when they arrived, he was delighted and at once drank with them; in a short while Hong arrived, and he was not offended either.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had a foot ailment and had one student and two sons carry him in a basket litter. When they arrived he was pleased and drank with them at once. Before long Hong arrived as well, and Qian showed no displeasure.

sentences.zh: 先是，顏延之為劉柳後軍功曹，在尋陽，與潛情款。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan Yanzhi was Rear Army Merit Officer to Liu Liu, stationed at Xunyang, and was on cordial terms with Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yan Yanzhi had served as Rear Army Merit Officer under Liu Liu at Xunyang and was on close terms with Qian.

sentences.zh: 後為始安郡，經過，日日造潛，每往必酣飲致醉。

translations.literal: Later he became governor of Shi'an commandery; passing through, he visited Qian every day, and each visit ended in deep drinking until drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as governor of Shi'an commandery, he passed through and visited Qian every day, each time drinking until thoroughly drunk.

sentences.zh: 臨去，留二萬錢與潛，潛悉送酒家，稍就取酒。

translations.literal: When leaving, he left twenty thousand cash with Qian; Qian sent it all to the wine shop and went from time to time to get wine.
translations.idiomatic: When he was leaving he left twenty thousand cash with Qian. Qian sent it all to the wine shop and went from time to time to draw wine.

sentences.zh: 嘗九月九日無酒，出宅邊菊叢中坐久，值弘送酒至，即便就酌，醉而後歸。

translations.literal: Once on the ninth day of the ninth month he had no wine; he went out and sat for a long time among the chrysanthemums beside his house. Just then Hong sent wine; he at once drank it and returned home drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the Double Ninth Festival he had no wine. He went out and sat for a long while among the chrysanthemums beside his house. Hong sent wine just then; he drank at once and returned home drunk.

sentences.zh: 潛不解音聲，而畜素琴一張，無弦，每有酒適，輒撫弄以寄其意。

translations.literal: Qian did not understand music and tones, yet he kept one plain zither without strings; whenever wine suited him, he would stroke and play it to lodge his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qian did not understand music, yet he kept a plain stringless zither; whenever he had wine to his liking, he would stroke it to give voice to his feelings.

sentences.zh: 貴賤造之者，有酒輒設，潛若先醉，便語客：「我醉欲眠，卿可去。」

translations.literal: Whether noble or base, whoever visited him—if there was wine he would set it out. If Qian got drunk first, he would tell his guest: "I am drunk and wish to sleep; you may go."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever visited him, noble or humble, he would serve wine if he had any. If Qian got drunk first, he would tell his guest, "I am drunk and wish to sleep—you may go."

sentences.zh: 其真率如此。

translations.literal: His sincerity and candor were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his sincerity and candor.

sentences.zh: 郡將候潛值其酒熟，取頭上葛巾漉酒，畢，還復著之。

translations.literal: The prefect awaiting Qian happened upon his wine being ready; he took the hemp kerchief from his head to strain the wine, and when finished put it back on.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect came to call on Qian and found his wine ready, he took the hemp kerchief from his head to strain it, then put the kerchief back on when he was done.

sentences.zh: 潛弱年薄官，不潔去就之跡。

translations.literal: In his youth Qian held minor posts and did not keep his coming and going unsullied.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Qian held minor office and did not keep a spotless record of withdrawal and return.

sentences.zh: 自以曾祖晉世宰輔，恥復屈身後代，自高祖王業漸隆，不復肯仕。

translations.literal: Considering that his great-grandfather had been a chief minister in the Jin dynasty, he was ashamed to bow again to a later age; from the time when Emperor Gaozu's royal enterprise gradually rose, he no longer consented to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Because his great-grandfather had served as chief minister under Jin, he was ashamed to submit again to a later dynasty. From the time Emperor Gaozu's royal enterprise began to rise, he would serve no more.

sentences.zh: 所著文章，皆題其年月，義熙以前，則書晉氏年號；

translations.literal: In all the writings he composed, he marked the year and month; before Yixi he wrote the Jin dynasty's era names;
translations.idiomatic: In all his writings he dated each piece by year and month. Before the Yixi era he recorded the Jin dynasty's reign titles;

sentences.zh: 自永初以來，唯云甲子而已。

translations.literal: From Yongchu onward he only wrote the cyclic stem-branch.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yongchu era onward he wrote only the sexagenary cycle year.

sentences.zh: 與子書以言其志，並為訓戒曰：

translations.literal: In a letter to his son he stated his intent and also gave admonitions, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In a letter to his son he set forth his aims and gave admonitions as follows:

sentences.zh: 天地賦命，有往必終，自古賢聖，誰能獨免。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth confer life; where there is going forth there must be an end—from antiquity what sage or worthy has been able alone to escape?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth confer life; all who go forth must come to an end—from antiquity what sage or worthy has ever escaped alone?

sentences.zh: 子夏言曰：「死生有命，富貴在天。」

translations.literal: Zixia said: "Life and death have fate; wealth and honor are in Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zixia said, "Life and death are ordained by fate; wealth and honor lie in Heaven's hands."

sentences.zh: 四友之人，親受音旨，發斯談者，豈非窮達不可妄求，壽夭永無外請故邪。

translations.literal: The men among the four friends personally received his message; he who uttered this discourse—was it not because advancement and obscurity cannot be rashly sought, and long life and early death can never be prayed for from without?
translations.idiomatic: The men among Confucius's four associates personally received this teaching. Was it not because success and failure cannot be rashly sought, and long life and early death cannot be begged from without?

sentences.zh: 吾年過五十，而窮苦荼毒，家貧弊，東西遊走。

translations.literal: My years pass fifty, yet I suffer bitter hardship; my household is poor and worn, drifting east and west.
translations.idiomatic: I am past fifty, yet I suffer bitter hardship; my household is poor and worn, and I drift from place to place.

sentences.zh: 性剛才拙，與物多忤，自量為己，必貽俗患，僶俛辭世，使汝幼而饑寒耳。

translations.literal: By nature I am stiff and my talent clumsy; I clash much with things. Measuring for myself, I was sure to bring worldly trouble; bowing low I left the world, making you suffer hunger and cold while still young.
translations.idiomatic: My nature is stiff and my talents clumsy; I clash often with the world. I knew I would bring trouble upon myself, so I bowed out of public life—leaving you to know hunger and cold while still young.

sentences.zh: 常感孺仲賢妻之言，敗絮自擁，何慚兒子。

translations.literal: I am often moved by the worthy wife of Ruzhong's words: "Warming myself in ragged cotton—what shame before my sons?"
translations.idiomatic: I am often moved by the words of Ruzhong's worthy wife: "Wrapped in ragged cotton—what shame is there before one's sons?"

sentences.zh: 此既一事矣。

translations.literal: This is already one matter.
translations.idiomatic: That is one consolation.

sentences.zh: 但恨鄰靡二仲，室無萊婦，抱茲苦心，良獨罔罔。

translations.literal: Only I regret having no two Zhongs among my neighbors, no Laifu wife in my house—bearing this bitter heart, truly I am alone and desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I regret that I have no Zhong brothers among my neighbors and no Laifu wife in my house; bearing this bitter heart, I am utterly alone and adrift.

sentences.zh: 少年來好書，偶愛閒靜，開卷有得，便欣然忘食。

translations.literal: From youth I have loved books, and by chance loved quiet; opening a scroll and gaining something, I would gladly forget to eat.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I have loved books and cherished quiet; whenever I opened a scroll and found something worth having, I forgot to eat for joy.

sentences.zh: 見樹木交廕，時鳥變聲，亦復歡爾有喜。

translations.literal: Seeing trees shade one another and seasonal birds shift their voices, I would likewise rejoice and feel glad.
translations.idiomatic: When I saw trees casting shade upon one another and seasonal birds changing their songs, I would rejoice in the same way.

sentences.zh: 嘗言五六月北窗下臥，遇涼風暫至，自謂是羲皇上人。

translations.literal: He once said that lying beneath the north window in the fifth and sixth months, when a cool breeze came for a moment, he considered himself a man of the age of Fuxi the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that lying beneath the north window in the fifth and sixth months, when a cool breeze came briefly, he felt himself a man of the age of Fuxi.

sentences.zh: 意淺識陋，日月遂往，緬求在昔，眇然如何。

translations.literal: My intent was shallow and my understanding crude; days and months have passed. Looking back to the past—how distant and dim!
translations.idiomatic: My thoughts were shallow and my understanding crude; days and months have flown. Looking back to the past—how remote it has become!

sentences.zh: 疾患以來，漸就衰損，親舊不遺，每以藥石見救，自恐大分將有限也。

translations.literal: Since illness began I have gradually declined; relatives and friends have not abandoned me and often brought medicine to save me, yet I fear my allotted span will soon be limited.
translations.idiomatic: Since my illness began I have gradually weakened. Relatives and friends have not abandoned me and often sent remedies, yet I fear my allotted span draws near its limit.

sentences.zh: 恨汝輩稚小，家貧無役，柴水之勞，何時可免，念之在心，若何可言。

translations.literal: I regret that you are still young, the house is poor with no servants—the toil of gathering firewood and drawing water, when can it be escaped? Thinking of it in the heart—how can it be told?
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that you are still young, our household is poor and has no servants—the toil of firewood and water, when will you be free of it? The thought fills my heart beyond words.

sentences.zh: 然雖不同生，當思四海皆弟兄之義。

translations.literal: Yet although not born of the same mother, you should bear in mind the principle that within the four seas all are brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though you were not born of the same mother, remember that within the four seas all men are brothers.

sentences.zh: 鮑叔、敬仲，分財無猜；

translations.literal: Baoshu and Jingzhong divided wealth without suspicion;
translations.idiomatic: Baoshu and Jingzhong divided wealth without mistrust;

sentences.zh: 歸生、伍舉，班荊道舊，遂能以敗為成，因喪立功。

translations.literal: Guisheng and Wu Ju, spreading thorns and speaking of old times, thus were able to turn defeat into victory and through disaster achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Guisheng and Wu Ju, breaking thorns and renewing old friendship, thereby turned defeat into victory and won merit from disaster.

sentences.zh: 他人尚爾，況共父之人哉！

translations.literal: Other men were still thus—how much more those of the same father!
translations.idiomatic: If others could do as much, how much more should those who share one father!

sentences.zh: 潁川韓元長，漢末名士，身處卿佐，八十而終，兄弟同居，至於沒齒。

translations.literal: Han Yuanchang of Yingchuan, a famed scholar at the end of Han, though occupying ministerial rank, died at eighty; brothers dwelt together until the end of their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuanchang of Yingchuan, a renowned scholar of the late Han, though he held high office lived to eighty; he and his brothers dwelt together until the end of their days.

sentences.zh: 濟北氾稚春，晉時操行人也，七世同財，家人無怨色。

translations.literal: Fan Zhichun of Jibei was a man of upright conduct in the Jin; seven generations shared wealth, and the family showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhichun of Jibei was a man of upright conduct in Jin times; seven generations held property in common, and not one in the family bore resentment.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「高山仰止，景行行止。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "The high mountain—look up to it; the great roadway—walk upon it."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Look up to the high mountain; walk in the broad way."

sentences.zh: 汝其慎哉！

translations.literal: You must be careful!
translations.idiomatic: Take heed!

sentences.zh: 吾復何言。

translations.literal: What more can I say?
translations.idiomatic: What more can I say?

sentences.zh: 又為《命子詩》以貽之曰：

translations.literal: He also composed "Poem to Command the Son" and presented it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also composed the "Poem to Command the Son" and presented it as follows:

sentences.zh: 悠悠我祖，爰自陶唐。

translations.literal: Distant, distant is my ancestor, from Yaotang of Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Distant, distant is my ancestor, from Yaotang of Tao.

sentences.zh: 邈為虞賓，歷世垂光。

translations.literal: Far off as a guest of Yu, passing generations he let down his light.
translations.idiomatic: Far off as a guest of Yu, passing generations he let down his light.

sentences.zh: 御龍勤夏，豕韋翼商。

translations.literal: Dragon-tamer served Xia; Shiwei aided Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-tamer served Xia; Shiwei aided Shang.

sentences.zh: 穆穆司徒，厥族以昌。

translations.literal: Solemn was the Minister of Education; his clan thereby flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn was the Minister of Education; his clan thereby flourished.

sentences.zh: 紛紜戰國，漠漠衰周。

translations.literal: Tumultuous the Warring States; dim and fading Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tumultuous the Warring States; dim and fading Zhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳隱於林，幽人在丘。

translations.literal: The phoenix hides in the forest; the recluse dwells on the hill.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix hides in the forest; the recluse dwells on the hill.

sentences.zh: 逸虯撓云，奔鯨駭流。

translations.literal: The roaming dragon bends the clouds; the racing whale terrifies the stream.
translations.idiomatic: The roaming dragon bends the clouds; the racing whale terrifies the stream.

sentences.zh: 天集有漢，眷予湣侯。

translations.literal: Heaven gathered Han; it favored our Marquis Min.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gathered Han; it favored our Marquis Min.

sentences.zh: 於赫湣侯，運當攀龍。

translations.literal: Splendid the Marquis Min—his fortune was to mount the dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid the Marquis Min—his fortune was to mount the dragon.

sentences.zh: 撫劍夙邁，顯茲武功。

translations.literal: He grasped his sword and set out early, displaying this martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He grasped his sword and set out early, displaying this martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 參誓山河，啟土開封。

translations.literal: He shared in swearing by rivers and mountains, opened land and received Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in swearing by rivers and mountains, opened land and received Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 亹亹丞相，允迪前蹤。

translations.literal: Diligent the Chancellor, truly following the tracks before.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent the Chancellor, truly following the tracks before.

sentences.zh: 渾渾長源，蔚蔚洪柯。

translations.literal: Vast the long source; luxuriant the great trunk.
translations.idiomatic: Vast the long source; luxuriant the great trunk.

sentences.zh: 群川載導，眾條載羅。

translations.literal: Myriad streams conduct forth; countless branches spread in array.
translations.idiomatic: Myriad streams conduct forth; countless branches spread in array.

sentences.zh: 時有默語，運固隆汙。

translations.literal: Times have silence and speech; fortune is indeed rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Times have silence and speech; fortune is indeed rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 在我中晉，業融長沙。

translations.literal: In our mid-Jin, the enterprise prospered at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In our mid-Jin, the enterprise prospered at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 桓桓長沙，伊勳伊德。

translations.literal: Majestic Changsha—both merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Majestic Changsha—both merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 天子疇我，專征南國。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven chose me; I was charged to campaign alone in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven chose me; I was charged to campaign alone in the south.

sentences.zh: 功遂辭歸，臨寵不惑。

translations.literal: Merit achieved, I declined and returned; facing favor I was not deluded.
translations.idiomatic: Merit achieved, I declined and returned; facing favor I was not deluded.

sentences.zh: 孰謂斯心，而可近得。

translations.literal: Who would say this heart could be closely attained?
translations.idiomatic: Who would say this heart could be closely attained?

sentences.zh: 肅矣我祖，慎終如始。

translations.literal: Solemn is my ancestor, careful at the end as at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn is my ancestor, careful at the end as at the beginning.

sentences.zh: 直方二台，惠和千里。

translations.literal: Upright at both terraces, kind and harmonious for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Upright at both terraces, kind and harmonious for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 於皇仁考，淡焉虛止。

translations.literal: Grand is my benevolent father; calmly he dwelt in emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Grand is my benevolent father; calmly he dwelt in emptiness.

sentences.zh: 寄跡夙運，冥茲慍喜。

translations.literal: He left his traces to early fortune; oblivious to anger and joy.
translations.idiomatic: He left his traces to early fortune; oblivious to anger and joy.

sentences.zh: 嗟餘寡陋，瞻望靡及。

translations.literal: Alas, I am meager and crude; gazing up I cannot reach.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, I am meager and crude; gazing up I cannot reach.

sentences.zh: 顧慚華鬢，負景只立。

translations.literal: Turning back I blush at my gray temples, standing alone in reflected shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back I blush at my gray temples, standing alone in reflected shadow.

sentences.zh: 三千之罪，無後其急。

translations.literal: Among the three thousand offenses, having no successor is most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Among the three thousand offenses, having no successor is most urgent.

sentences.zh: 我誠念哉，呱聞爾泣。

translations.literal: I truly think of it—at your first cry I heard you weep.
translations.idiomatic: I truly think of it—at your first cry I heard you weep.

sentences.zh: 卜云嘉日，占爾良時。

translations.literal: The oracle tells an auspicious day; divination marks your good hour.
translations.idiomatic: The oracle tells an auspicious day; divination marks your good hour.

sentences.zh: 名爾曰儼，字爾求思。

translations.literal: I name you Yan; I style you Qiusi ("Seeking Thought").
translations.idiomatic: I name you Yan; I style you Qiusi ("Seeking Thought").

sentences.zh: 溫恭朝夕，念茲在茲。

translations.literal: Be warm and respectful morning and evening; keep this thought ever present.
translations.idiomatic: Be warm and respectful morning and evening; keep this thought ever present.

sentences.zh: 尚想孔伋，庶其企而。

translations.literal: Still I think of Kong Ji; perhaps you will strive toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Still I think of Kong Ji; perhaps you will strive toward him.

sentences.zh: 厲夜生子，遽而求火。

translations.literal: At night when a child was born in urgency, one rushed to seek fire.
translations.idiomatic: At night when a child was born in urgency, one rushed to seek fire.

sentences.zh: 凡百有心，奚待於我。

translations.literal: All who have heart—why wait for me?
translations.idiomatic: All who have heart—why wait for me?

sentences.zh: 既見其生，實欲其可。

translations.literal: Having seen him born, I truly wish him to be capable.
translations.idiomatic: Having seen him born, I truly wish him to be capable.

sentences.zh: 人亦有言，斯情無假。

translations.literal: People also have a saying—this feeling has no falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: People also have a saying—this feeling has no falsehood.

sentences.zh: 日居月諸，漸免於孩。

translations.literal: Days pass and months go; gradually you free yourself from infancy.
translations.idiomatic: Days pass and months go; gradually you free yourself from infancy.

sentences.zh: 福不虛至，禍亦易來。

translations.literal: Fortune does not come in vain; misfortune likewise comes easily.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune does not come in vain; misfortune likewise comes easily.

sentences.zh: 夙興夜寐，願爾斯才。

translations.literal: Rise early and sleep late—I wish you this talent.
translations.idiomatic: Rise early and sleep late—I wish you this talent.

sentences.zh: 爾之不才，亦已焉哉。

translations.literal: If you lack talent—so be it.
translations.idiomatic: If you lack talent—so be it.

sentences.zh: 潛元嘉四年卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Qian died in the fourth year of Yuanjia, at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Qian died in the fourth year of Yuanjia, at age sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 宗彧之，字叔粲，南陽涅陽人，炳從父弟也。

translations.literal: Zong Yuzhi, styled Shucan, was a man of Nieyang in Nanyang, a younger cousin of Bing on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yuzhi, styled Shucan, was a man of Nieyang in Nanyang, a younger cousin of Bing on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 蚤孤，事兄恭謹，家貧好學，雖文義不逮炳，而真澹過之。

translations.literal: He lost his parents early, served his elder brother with reverence and care, and though poor loved learning; though he did not match Bing in literary refinement, he surpassed him in genuineness and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he served his elder brother with reverence and care. Though poor, he loved learning; he did not match Bing in literary refinement, but surpassed him in genuineness and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Prefectural Secretary and recommended him as Presented Scholar; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province summoned him as Prefectural Secretary and recommended him as Presented Scholar; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 公私餼遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: From public or private sources, gifts and presents—he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts from public or private sources—he accepted none.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，徵著作佐郎，不至。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was summoned as Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was summoned as Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section but did not come.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，大使陸子真觀采風俗，三詣彧之，每辭疾不見也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, the envoy Lu Zizhen was sent to observe local customs; three times he called on Yuzhi, and each time Yuzhi pleaded illness and refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia, the envoy Lu Zizhen was sent to observe local customs. Three times he called on Yuzhi, and each time Yuzhi pleaded illness and refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 告人曰：「我布衣草萊之人，少長壟畝，何枉軒冕之客。」

translations.literal: He told others: "I am a man of hemp cloth and field grass, who grew up long among furrows—why should honored guests in carriage caps bother me?"
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "I am a man of hemp cloth who grew up among the furrows—why should honored guests in carriage caps bother with me?"

sentences.zh: 子真還，表薦之，徵員外散騎侍郎，又不就。

translations.literal: Zizhen on returning memorialized recommending him; he was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section, and again he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, Zizhen memorialized recommending him. He was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section, and again he declined.

sentences.zh: 元嘉八年，卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia he died, at age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia he died, at age fifty.

sentences.zh: 沈道虔，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Daoqian was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Daoqian was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 少仁愛，好《老》、《易》，居縣北石山下。

translations.literal: From youth he was benevolent and loving; he loved the Laozi and the Changes, and dwelt beneath Stone Mountain north of the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was benevolent and loving. He loved the Laozi and the Changes and dwelt beneath Stone Mountain north of the county seat.

sentences.zh: 孫恩亂後饑荒，縣令庾肅之迎出縣南廢頭裏，為立小宅，臨溪，有山水之玩。

translations.literal: After Sun En's rebellion there was famine; Magistrate Yu Suzhi brought him out to Feitouli south of the county and built a small dwelling for him by a stream, with the pleasures of mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun En's rebellion brought famine, Magistrate Yu Suzhi brought him out to Feitouli south of the county and built a small dwelling for him by a stream, with the pleasures of mountains and waters.

sentences.zh: 時復還石山精廬，與諸孤兄子共釜庾之資，困不改節。

translations.literal: From time to time he would return to his hermitage on Stone Mountain and share his store of grain with his orphaned elder brother's sons; in hardship he did not alter his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he returned to his hermitage on Stone Mountain and shared his store of grain with his orphaned elder brother's sons; in hardship he did not alter his integrity.

sentences.zh: 受琴於戴逵，王敬弘深敬之。

translations.literal: He received the zither from Dai Kui; Wang Jinghong deeply respected him.
translations.idiomatic: He received instruction in the zither from Dai Kui; Wang Jinghong deeply respected him.

sentences.zh: 郡州府凡十二命，皆不就。

translations.literal: From commandery, province, and prefecture there were twelve appointments in all; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery, province, and prefecture together issued twelve appointments; he accepted none.

sentences.zh: 有人竊其園萊者，還見之，乃自逃隱，待竊者取足去後乃出。

translations.literal: Once someone was stealing vegetables from his garden; when Daoqian returned and saw it, he hid himself until the thief had taken enough and left, then came out.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone was stealing vegetables from his garden. When Daoqian returned and saw it, he hid himself until the thief had taken enough and left, then came out.

sentences.zh: 人拔其屋後筍，令人止之，曰：「惜此筍欲令成林，更有佳者相與。」

translations.literal: People pulled the bamboo shoots behind his house; he had someone stop them, saying: "I cherish these shoots and wish them to become a grove; I will share finer ones with you."
translations.idiomatic: People pulled the bamboo shoots behind his house. He had someone stop them, saying, "I cherish these shoots and wish them to become a grove—I will share finer ones with you."

sentences.zh: 乃令人買大筍送與之。

translations.literal: He then had someone buy large bamboo shoots and send them to them.
translations.idiomatic: He then had someone buy large bamboo shoots and send them to the gatherers.

sentences.zh: 盜者慚不取，道虔使置其門內而還。

translations.literal: The thief was ashamed and would not take them; Daoqian had them placed inside his gate and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was ashamed and would not take them; Daoqian had them placed inside his gate and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 常以捃拾自資，同捃者爭穟，道虔諫之不止，悉以其所得與之，爭者愧恧。

translations.literal: He often supported himself by gathering fallen grain; when fellow gatherers fought over ears of grain, Daoqian remonstrated without success and gave them all he had gathered; the quarrelers felt ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: He often supported himself by gathering fallen grain. When fellow gatherers fought over ears of grain, Daoqian remonstrated without success and gave them all he had gathered; the quarrelers felt ashamed.

sentences.zh: 後每爭，輒云：「勿令居士知。」

translations.literal: Afterward whenever they quarreled they would say: "Don't let the lay devotee know."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward whenever they quarreled they would say, "Don't let the lay devotee know."

sentences.zh: 冬月無復衣，戴顒聞而迎之，為作衣服，並與錢一萬。

translations.literal: In winter he had no more clothes; Dai Yong heard and fetched him, made clothes for him, and gave him ten thousand cash as well.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he had no more clothes. Dai Yong heard of it, fetched him, made clothes for him, and gave him ten thousand cash as well.

sentences.zh: 既還，分身上衣及錢，悉供諸兄弟子無衣者。

translations.literal: When he returned, he divided his upper garment and the money and gave them all to his brothers' sons who had no clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he divided his upper garment and the money and gave them all to his brothers' sons who had no clothes.

sentences.zh: 鄉里年少，相率受學。

translations.literal: The young men of the village one after another came to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: The young men of the village came one after another to study under him.

sentences.zh: 道虔常無食，無以立學徒。

translations.literal: Daoqian often had no food and no means to support his students.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian often had no food and no means to support his students.

sentences.zh: 武康令孔欣之厚相資給，受業者咸得有成。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Wukang, Kong Xinzhi, generously supported and supplied him; all who studied under him were able to achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Kong Xinzhi of Wukang generously supported him, and all who studied under him were able to succeed.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，遣使存問，賜錢三萬，米二百斛，悉以嫁娶孤兄子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu heard of this, he sent an envoy to inquire after him and bestowed thirty thousand cash and two hundred bushels of grain, all of which he used to marry off his orphaned elder brother's sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu heard of this, he sent an envoy to inquire after him and bestowed thirty thousand cash and two hundred bushels of grain, all of which he used to marry off his orphaned elder brother's sons.

sentences.zh: 征員外散騎侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section but declined.

sentences.zh: 累世事佛，推父祖舊宅為寺。

translations.literal: For generations the family had served Buddhism; he converted his father and grandfather's old residence into a temple.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served Buddhism for generations; he converted his forefathers' old residence into a temple.

sentences.zh: 至四月八日，每請像。

translations.literal: On reaching the eighth day of the fourth month, he would each time invite an image.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month each year, he would invite a Buddha image for veneration.

sentences.zh: 請像之日，輒舉家感慟焉。

translations.literal: On the day when the image was invited, the whole family was always deeply moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the image was invited, the whole family would be deeply moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 道虔年老，菜食，恆無經日之資，而琴書為樂，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Daoqian in old age ate only vegetables, constantly lacking resources to last a day, yet he took the zither and books as his pleasure and never slackened his efforts.
translations.idiomatic: In old age Daoqian lived on vegetables and often lacked enough to last a day, yet he took pleasure in the zither and books and never slackened his efforts.

sentences.zh: 太祖敕郡縣令，隨時資給。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu ordered the commandery and county magistrates to supply him as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu ordered the commandery and county magistrates to provide for him as needed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，卒，時年八十二。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he died, at age eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he died, at age eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 子慧鋒，脩父業，辟從事，皆不就。

translations.literal: His son Huifeng continued his father's work; summoned as Staff Member, he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huifeng continued his father's work; summoned as Staff Member, he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 郭希林，武昌武昌人也。

translations.literal: Guo Xilin was a man of Wuchang in Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xilin was a man of Wuchang in Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖翻，晉世高尚不仕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fan was lofty in integrity and did not serve under the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fan was lofty in integrity and did not serve under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 希林少守家業，征州主簿，秀才，衛軍參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: Xilin in youth maintained the family estate; summoned as Provincial Chief Clerk, Presented Scholar, and Staff Member of the Guard Army, he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xilin maintained the family estate; summoned as Provincial Chief Clerk, Presented Scholar, and Staff Member of the Guard Army, he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，吏部尚書王敬弘舉王弘之為太子庶子，希林為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, Minister of Personnel Wang Jinghong recommended Wang Hongzhi as Teacher of the Crown Prince and Xilin as Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia, Minister of Personnel Wang Jinghong recommended Wang Hongzhi as Teacher of the Crown Prince and Xilin as Assistant Gentleman in the Writing Section.

sentences.zh: 後又征員外散騎侍郎，並不就。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section but declined.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, at age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died, at age forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子蒙，亦隱居不仕。

translations.literal: His son Meng also lived in seclusion and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: His son Meng also lived in seclusion and did not serve.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，郢州刺史蔡興宗辟為主簿，不就。

translations.literal: During the Taishi era, Cai Xingzong, Inspector of Yingzhou, recruited him as Chief Clerk; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era, Cai Xingzong, Inspector of Yingzhou, recruited him as Chief Clerk; he declined.

sentences.zh: 雷次宗，字仲倫，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Lei Cizong, styled Zhonglun, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Cizong, styled Zhonglun, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 少入廬山，事沙門釋慧遠，篤志好學，尤明《三禮》、《毛詩》，隱退不交世務。

translations.literal: From youth he entered Mount Lu and served the monk Shi Huiyuan; steadfast in purpose and devoted to learning, he was especially versed in the Three Rites and the Mao Commentary on the Odes, living in withdrawal without mixing in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he entered Mount Lu and studied under the monk Shi Huiyuan; steadfast in purpose and devoted to learning, he was especially versed in the Three Rites and the Mao Commentary on the Odes, living in withdrawal without mixing in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 本州辟從事，員外散騎侍郎征，並不就。

translations.literal: Recruited by his province as Staff Member and summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section, he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited by his province as Staff Member and summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section, he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 與子侄書以言所守，曰：

translations.literal: In a letter to his sons and nephews he spoke of what he upheld, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In a letter to his sons and nephews he spoke of what he upheld, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫生之脩短，咸有定分，定分之外，不可以智力求，但當於所稟之中，順而勿率耳。

translations.literal: As for whether life is long or short, all have a fixed allotment; beyond that allotment one cannot seek by wit or strength—one should only within what one has received follow along and not rush ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Whether life is long or short, each person has a fixed allotment; beyond that one cannot strive by wit or force—one should only follow what fate has granted and not rush ahead.

sentences.zh: 吾少嬰羸患，事鐘養疾，為性好閑，志棲物表，故雖在童稚之年，已懷遠跡之意。

translations.literal: From youth I was afflicted with frail illness; my affairs centered on nursing sickness; my nature loves leisure and my will settles beyond worldly things—thus though still in childhood I already harbored the intent to withdraw far away.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I suffered frail illness and my days centered on nursing my health; my nature loves quiet and my will rests beyond the things of the world—thus even in childhood I already cherished the wish to withdraw far from society.

sentences.zh: 暨於弱冠，遂托業廬山，逮事釋和尚。

translations.literal: When I reached weak-cap, I entrusted myself to Mount Lu and came to serve Master Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When I reached twenty I committed myself to Mount Lu and became a disciple of Master Shi [Huiyuan].

sentences.zh: 於時師友淵源，務訓弘道，外慕等夷，內懷悱發，於是洗氣神明，玩心墳典，勉志勤躬，夜以繼日。

translations.literal: At that time teachers and friends were deep and numerous, devoted to instruction and spreading the Way; outwardly we admired equality, inwardly we harbored urgent aspiration—thus we purified our spirits, took delight in the classics, strove in purpose and diligence, continuing day into night.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers and friends were then abundant and devoted to instruction and spreading the Way; outwardly we esteemed equality, inwardly we burned with aspiration—we purified our spirits, took delight in the classics, and strove day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 爰有山水之好，悟言之歡，實足以通理輔性，成夫亹亹之業，樂以忘憂，不知朝日之晏矣。

translations.literal: Then there was love of mountains and waters and the joy of enlightened discourse—truly enough to penetrate principle and assist character, to accomplish earnest study, finding joy that banished sorrow, unaware that the morning sun had grown late.
translations.idiomatic: There was the love of mountains and waters and the joy of enlightened discourse—enough truly to penetrate principle and nurture character, to carry on earnest study, finding such joy that sorrow was forgotten and one was unaware the morning sun had already grown late.

sentences.zh: 自遊道餐風，二十餘載，淵匠既傾，良朋凋索，續以釁逆違天，備嘗荼蓼，疇昔誠願，頓盡一朝，心慮荒散，情意衰損，故遂與汝曹歸耕壟畔，山居谷飲，人理久絕。

translations.literal: Since roaming the Way and dining on wind for more than twenty years, the deep craftsmen have already fallen and good friends withered away; then came rebellion against Heaven and I tasted every bitterness—all former sincere aspirations vanished in a day, my mind scattered and my feelings depleted; therefore I have returned with you all to plow beside the fields, dwelling in mountains and drinking from valleys, long cut off from human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since I began roaming the Way and living on wind and dew more than twenty years ago, my master has fallen and good friends have been lost; then rebellion against Heaven brought every bitterness—former aspirations vanished overnight, my mind scattered and my spirits depleted; so I have returned with you all to plow the fields, living in the mountains and drinking from the valleys, long severed from human affairs.

sentences.zh: 日月不處，忽復十年，犬馬之齒，已逾知命。

translations.literal: Days and months do not stay; suddenly ten years have passed again; the teeth of dog and horse have already passed fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Days and months wait for no one; suddenly another ten years have passed, and I have already passed fifty.

sentences.zh: 崦嵫將迫，前塗幾何，實遠想尚子五嶽之舉，近謝居室瑣瑣之勤。

translations.literal: Sunset is nearing—how much road lies ahead! I truly think from afar of Master Shang's journey to the Five Peaks and from near at hand decline the petty toils of household life.
translations.idiomatic: Sunset draws near—how much road remains? I think from afar of Master Shang's journey to the Five Peaks and from near at hand renounce the petty labors of household life.

sentences.zh: 及今耄未至惛，衰不及頓，尚可厲志於所期，縱心於所托，棲誠來生之津梁，專氣莫年之攝養，玩歲日於良辰，偷餘樂於將除，在心所期，盡於此矣。

translations.literal: While old age has not yet brought confusion and decline has not yet been sudden, one can still strengthen resolve toward what one hopes for and let the heart roam toward what one trusts in—dwelling in sincerity on the bridge to the next life, concentrating one's qi in the nourishment of one's late years, passing the days in good seasons, stealing leftover joy before the end comes; what the heart hopes for is all fulfilled in this.
translations.idiomatic: While senility has not yet brought confusion and decline has not yet struck suddenly, one can still strengthen the resolve one has cherished and give free rein to what one trusts in—dwelling in sincerity on the bridge to the next life, concentrating one's vital force in the care of one's final years, passing days at their best, stealing what joy remains before the end; all that the heart can hope for is fulfilled in this.

sentences.zh: 汝等年各成長，冠娶已畢，脩惜衡泌，吾復何憂。

translations.literal: You all have each grown up; capping and marriage are finished; you cherish study and hold to the hermit's path—I have nothing more to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: You have all come of age, finished capping and marriage, and cherish a life of study and reclusion—what more have I to worry about?

sentences.zh: 但顧守全所志，以保令終耳。

translations.literal: I only hope you guard and preserve your aspirations, to secure a good end.
translations.idiomatic: I only ask that you keep your aspirations intact and so end your days well.

sentences.zh: 自今以往，家事大小，一勿見關，子平之言，可以為法。

translations.literal: From now on, great or small in household affairs, do not involve me at all—the words of Ziping may serve as a model.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, in household affairs great or small, do not involve me at all—let Ziping's example be your guide.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十五年，征次宗至京師，開館於雞籠山，聚徒教授，置生百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia, Cizong was summoned to the capital, opened a school on Cockcage Mountain, gathered disciples to teach, and enrolled more than a hundred students.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia, Cizong was summoned to the capital, opened a school on Cockcage Mountain, gathered disciples to teach, and enrolled more than a hundred students.

sentences.zh: 會稽硃膺之、潁川庾蔚之並以儒學，監總諸生。

translations.literal: Zhu Yingzhi of Kuaiji and Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, both renowned for Confucian learning, supervised all the students.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingzhi of Kuaiji and Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, both renowned for Confucian learning, supervised all the students.

sentences.zh: 時國子學未立，上留心藝術，使丹陽尹何尚之立玄學，太子率更令何承天立史學，司徒參軍謝元立文學，凡四學並建。

translations.literal: At the time the Imperial Academy had not yet been established; the emperor attended to the arts and sciences, had the Administrator of Danyang He Shangzhi establish the School of Dark Learning, the Heir Apparent's Director of Palace Manufactures He Chengtian establish the School of History, and Staff Member to the Minister Over the Masses Xie Yuan establish the School of Letters—in all four schools were established together.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Imperial Academy had not yet been established; the emperor attended to the arts and sciences, had Danyang Administrator He Shangzhi establish the School of Dark Learning, Heir Apparent's Director of Palace Manufactures He Chengtian establish the School of History, and Staff Member to the Minister Over the Masses Xie Yuan establish the School of Letters—in all four schools were established together.

sentences.zh: 車駕數幸次宗學館，資給甚厚。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage several times visited Cizong's school; support was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor several times visited Cizong's school; support was very generous.

sentences.zh: 又除給事中，不就。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Attendant Within the Gates; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Attendant Within the Gates but declined.

sentences.zh: 久之，還廬山，公卿以下，並設祖道。

translations.literal: After some time he returned to Mount Lu; from dukes and ministers downward, all arranged farewell banquets.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he returned to Mount Lu; from dukes and ministers downward, all arranged farewell banquets for him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，詔曰：「前新除給事中雷次宗，篤尚希古，經行明脩，自絕招命，守志隱約。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year an edict said: "The former newly appointed Attendant Within the Gates Lei Cizong, deeply devoted to the ancient past, clear in conduct and cultivation, has of his own accord cut off summons, guarding his will in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year an edict declared: "The former newly appointed Attendant Within the Gates Lei Cizong, deeply devoted to the ancients, clear in conduct and self-cultivation, has of his own accord refused every summons and held to his will in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 宜加升引，以旌退素。

translations.literal: He should be further promoted and summoned, to commend his withdrawal and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: He should be further promoted and summoned, to honor his withdrawal and plain living.

sentences.zh: 可散騎侍郎。」

translations.literal: Let him be Attendant of Scattered Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Attendant of Scattered Cavalry."

sentences.zh: 後又征詣京邑，為築室於鐘山西巖下，謂之招隱館，使為皇太子諸王講《喪服》經。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned to the capital; a dwelling was built for him beneath the west cliff of Mount Zhong, called the Lodge for Summoning Recluses, and he was made to lecture the heir apparent and the princes on the Classic of Mourning Garments.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was again summoned to the capital; a dwelling was built for him beneath the west cliff of Mount Zhong, called the Lodge for Summoning Recluses, and he was made to lecture the heir apparent and the princes on the Classic of Mourning Garments.

sentences.zh: 次宗不入公門，乃使自華林東門入延賢堂就業。

translations.literal: Cizong would not enter the public gates, so he was made to enter the Hall for Extending Worthies from the east gate of Hualin to conduct his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Cizong would not enter the public gates, so he was made to enter the Hall for Extending Worthies from the east gate of Hualin to conduct his duties.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒於鐘山，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died on Mount Zhong, at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died on Mount Zhong, at age sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 太祖與江夏王義恭書道次宗亡，義恭答曰：「雷次宗不救所疾，甚可痛念。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu wrote to Prince Jiangxia Yigong about Cizong's death; Yigong replied: "Lei Cizong could not be saved from his illness—deeply lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu wrote to Prince Jiangxia Yigong about Cizong's death; Yigong replied, "Lei Cizong could not be saved from his illness—deeply lamentable.

sentences.zh: 其幽棲窮藪，自賓聖朝，克己復禮，始終若一。

translations.literal: He dwelt in secluded depths and remote thickets yet served the sagely court; restraining himself and returning to rites, beginning and end were as one.
translations.idiomatic: Though he dwelt in secluded depths and remote thickets, he served the sagely court; restraining himself and returning to rites, he was the same from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 伏惟天慈弘被，亦垂矜湣。」

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that heavenly kindness extends broadly and will also show pity and compassion."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully trust that heavenly kindness extends broadly and will also show pity and compassion."

sentences.zh: 子肅之，頗傳其業，官至豫章郡丞。

translations.literal: His son Suzhi largely transmitted his learning and reached the office of Assistant Magistrate of Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Suzhi largely transmitted his learning and reached the office of Assistant Magistrate of Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 硃百年，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Bainian was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bainian was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖愷之，晉右衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai was Right Guard General of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai was Right Guard General of Jin.

sentences.zh: 父濤，揚州主簿。

translations.literal: His father Tao was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 百年少有高情，親亡服闋，攜妻孔氏入會稽南山，以伐樵采箬為業。

translations.literal: Bainian from youth had lofty sentiments; when mourning for his parents ended he took his wife Lady Kong into the southern mountains of Kuaiji and made his livelihood by felling wood, gathering firewood, and picking bamboo leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Bainian from youth had lofty sentiments; when mourning for his parents ended he took his wife Lady Kong into the southern mountains of Kuaiji and made his livelihood by felling wood, gathering firewood, and picking bamboo leaves.

sentences.zh: 每以樵箬置道頭，輒為行人所取，明旦亦復如此。

translations.literal: Each time he placed firewood and bamboo leaves at the roadside, passersby would take them; the next morning it would happen again the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he placed firewood and bamboo leaves at the roadside, passersby would take them; the next morning the same thing would happen again.

sentences.zh: 人稍怪之，積久方知是硃隱士所賣，須者隨其所堪多少，留錢取樵箬而去。

translations.literal: People gradually found it strange; after a long time they learned it was the hermit Zhu selling goods—those who needed them would leave money according to what they could afford and take firewood or bamboo leaves.
translations.idiomatic: People gradually found it strange; after a long time they learned it was the hermit Zhu selling goods—those who needed them would leave money according to what they could afford and take firewood or bamboo leaves.

sentences.zh: 或遇寒雪，樵箬不售，無以自資，輒自搒船送妻還孔氏，天晴復迎之。

translations.literal: Sometimes when cold and snow came and firewood and bamboo leaves would not sell, with no means to support himself he would row a boat himself to send his wife back to the Kong family; when the weather cleared he would fetch her again.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when cold and snow came and firewood and bamboo leaves would not sell, with no means to support himself he would row a boat himself to send his wife back to the Kong family; when the weather cleared he would fetch her again.

sentences.zh: 有時出山陰為妻買繒彩三五尺，好飲酒，遇醉或失之。

translations.literal: Sometimes he went out to Shanyin to buy three or five feet of silk for his wife; he loved wine and when drunk would sometimes lose it.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he went out to Shanyin to buy three or five feet of silk for his wife; he loved wine and when drunk would sometimes lose it.

sentences.zh: 頗能言理，時為詩詠，往往有高勝之言。

translations.literal: He could speak on principle rather well and from time to time composed poetry; often there were lofty and surpassing words.
translations.idiomatic: He could speak on principle rather well and from time to time composed poetry; often there were lofty and surpassing words.

sentences.zh: 郡命功曹，州辟從事，舉秀才，並不就。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him Merit Officer, the province recruited him as Staff Member, and he was recommended as Presented Scholar; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery appointed him Merit Officer, the province recruited him as Staff Member, and he was recommended as Presented Scholar; he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 隱跡避人，唯與同縣孔覬友善。

translations.literal: He hid his traces and avoided people, befriending only Kong Yi of the same county.
translations.idiomatic: He hid his traces and avoided people, befriending only Kong Yi of the same county.

sentences.zh: 覬亦嗜酒，相得輒酣，對飲盡歡。

translations.literal: Yi also loved wine; when they met they would drink deeply, facing each other in full enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also loved wine; when they met they would drink deeply, facing each other in full enjoyment.

sentences.zh: 百年家素貧，母以冬月亡，衣並無絮，自此不衣綿帛。

translations.literal: Bainian's family had always been poor; his mother died in a winter month and her garments had no cotton padding—from then on he wore no silk or cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Bainian's family had always been poor; his mother died in a winter month and her garments had no cotton padding—from then on he wore no silk or cotton.

sentences.zh: 嘗寒時就覬宿，衣悉夾布，飲酒醉眠，覬以臥具覆之，百年不覺也。

translations.literal: Once in cold weather he stayed overnight at Yi's; his clothes were all unlined cloth; drunk from wine he fell asleep; Yi covered him with bedding but Bainian did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Once in cold weather he stayed overnight at Yi's; his clothes were all unlined cloth; drunk from wine he fell asleep; Yi covered him with bedding but Bainian did not notice.

sentences.zh: 既覺，引臥具去體，謂覬曰：「綿定奇溫。」

translations.literal: When he woke, he pulled the bedding away from his body and said to Yi: "Cotton is indeed wondrously warm."
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, he pulled the bedding away from his body and said to Yi, "Cotton is indeed wondrously warm."

sentences.zh: 因流涕悲慟，覬亦為之傷感。

translations.literal: He then wept in grief, and Yi also was moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: He then wept in grief, and Yi also was moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 王素，字休業，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Su, styled Xiuye, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, styled Xiuye, was a man of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 高祖翹之，晉光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qiaozhi was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qiaozhi was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness of Jin.

sentences.zh: 素少有志行，家貧母老。

translations.literal: Su from youth had resolve and conduct; his family was poor and his mother old.
translations.idiomatic: Su from youth had resolve and conduct; his family was poor and his mother old.

sentences.zh: 初為廬陵國侍郎，母憂去職。

translations.literal: Initially he served as Attendant in the Principality of Luling; when his mother died he left his post.
translations.idiomatic: Initially he served as Attendant in the Principality of Luling; when his mother died he left his post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，廬陵王紹為江州，親舊勸素脩完舊居，素不答，乃輕身往東陽，隱居不仕，頗營田園之資，得以自立。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Prince Shao of Luling was assigned to Jiangzhou; relatives and friends urged Su to restore his old residence; Su did not reply but went lightly to Dongyang, living in seclusion without serving; he managed fields and gardens to some extent and was able to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Prince Shao of Luling was assigned to Jiangzhou; relatives and friends urged Su to restore his old residence; Su did not reply but went lightly to Dongyang, living in seclusion without serving; he managed fields and gardens to some extent and was able to support himself.

sentences.zh: 愛好文義，不以人俗累懷。

translations.literal: He loved literature and principle and was not burdened in spirit by worldly vulgarity.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature and principle and was not burdened in spirit by worldly vulgarity.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，欲搜揚隱退，下詔曰：「濟世成務，咸達隱微，軌俗興讓，必表清節。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, wishing to seek out and promote the withdrawn, he issued an edict: "In aiding the age and accomplishing tasks, all should reach the hidden and subtle; in guiding custom and raising yielding, one must display pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, wishing to seek out and promote recluses, he issued an edict: "In aiding the age and accomplishing tasks, all should reach the hidden and subtle; in guiding custom and raising yielding, one must display pure integrity.

sentences.zh: 朕昧旦求善，思惇薄風，琅邪王素、會稽硃百年，並廉約貞遠，與物無競，自足皋畝，志在不移。

translations.literal: We at dawn seek the good, thinking to nurture simple ways—Wang Su of Langye and Zhu Bainian of Kuaiji, both frugal, plain, steadfast and distant, without contention with things, content upon the fields, their will unchanging.
translations.idiomatic: We at dawn seek the good, thinking to nurture simple ways—Wang Su of Langye and Zhu Bainian of Kuaiji, both frugal, plain, steadfast and distant, without contention with the world, content upon the fields, their will unchanging.

sentences.zh: 宜加褒引，以光難進。

translations.literal: They should be further commended and summoned, to glorify those hard to advance.
translations.idiomatic: They should be further commended and summoned, to honor those reluctant to advance.

sentences.zh: 並可太子舍子。」

translations.literal: Both may be made Household Attendants of the Heir."
translations.idiomatic: Both may be made Household Attendants of the Heir."

sentences.zh: 大明中，太宰江夏王義恭開府辟召，辟素為倉曹屬；

translations.literal: During the Daming era, Grand Preceptor Prince Jiangxia Yigong opened his staff and recruited; Su was recruited as Clerk of the Granary Section;
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era, Grand Preceptor Prince Jiangxia Yigong opened his staff and recruited; Su was recruited as Clerk of the Granary Section;

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始六年，又召為太子中舍人，並不就。

translations.literal: in the sixth year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong he was again summoned as Middle Household Attendant of the Heir; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong he was again summoned as Middle Household Attendant of the Heir; he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 素既屢被征辟，聲譽甚高。

translations.literal: Su having been repeatedly summoned and recruited, his renown was very high.
translations.idiomatic: Having been repeatedly summoned and recruited, Su's renown was very high.

sentences.zh: 山中有蚿蟲，聲清長，聽之使人不厭，而其形甚醜，素乃為《蚿賦》以自況。

translations.literal: In the mountains there is a millipede insect whose sound is clear and long—listening to it one does not tire, yet its form is very ugly; Su therefore wrote a "Rhapsody on the Millipede" to compare himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains there is a millipede whose call is clear and long—listening to it one does not tire, yet its form is very ugly; Su therefore wrote a "Rhapsody on the Millipede" to compare himself.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，時年五十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died, at age fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 時又有宋平劉睦之、汝南州韶、吳郡褚伯玉，亦隱身求志。

translations.literal: At the time there were also Liu Muzhi of Songping, Zhou Shao of Runan, and Chu Boyu of Wu commandery, who also concealed themselves to seek their will.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were also Liu Muzhi of Songping, Zhou Shao of Runan, and Chu Boyu of Wu commandery, who also concealed themselves to seek their will.

sentences.zh: 睦之居交州，除武平太守，不拜。

translations.literal: Muzhi lived in Jiaozhou; appointed Prefect of Wuping, he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi lived in Jiaozhou; appointed Prefect of Wuping, he declined.

sentences.zh: 韶字伯和，黃門侍郎文孫也。

translations.literal: Shao, styled Bohe, was grandson of Attendant Gentleman Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, styled Bohe, was grandson of Attendant Gentleman Wen.

sentences.zh: 築室湖孰之方山，征員外散騎侍郎，征北行參軍，不起。

translations.literal: He built a dwelling on Fang Mountain at Hushu; summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section and Acting Staff Member of the Northern Expedition, he would not rise to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He built a dwelling on Fang Mountain at Hushu; summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Exterior Service in the Cavalry Section and Acting Staff Member of the Northern Expedition, he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 伯玉居剡縣瀑布山三十餘載，揚州辟議曹從事，不就。

translations.literal: Boyu lived on Pubu Mountain in Shan county for more than thirty years; Yangzhou recruited him as Staff Member in the Bureau of Counsel; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu lived on Pubu Mountain in Shan county for more than thirty years; Yangzhou recruited him as Staff Member in the Bureau of Counsel; he declined.

sentences.zh: 關康之，字伯愉，河東楊人。

translations.literal: Guan Kangzhi, styled Boyu, was a man of Yang in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Kangzhi, styled Boyu, was a man of Yang in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世居京口，寓屬南平昌。

translations.literal: For generations his family resided at Jingkou, registered under Nanpingchang.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family resided at Jingkou, registered under Nanpingchang.

sentences.zh: 少而篤學，姿狀豐偉。

translations.literal: From youth he was devoted to learning; his bearing was large and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was devoted to learning; his bearing was large and imposing.

sentences.zh: 下邳趙繹以文義見稱，康之與之友善。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi of Xiapi was famed for literary learning; Kangzhi was friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi of Xiapi was famed for literary learning; Kangzhi was friendly with him.

sentences.zh: 特進顏延之見而知之。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Yan Yanzhi saw him and recognized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Yan Yanzhi saw him and recognized his talent.

sentences.zh: 晉陵顧悅之難王弼《易》義四十余條，康之申王難顧，遠有情理。

translations.literal: Gu Yuezhi of Jinling raised more than forty objections to Wang Bi's meanings in the Changes; Kangzhi upheld Wang and refuted Gu—far from superficial, there was genuine reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yuezhi of Jinling raised more than forty objections to Wang Bi's meanings in the Changes; Kangzhi upheld Wang and refuted Gu—far from superficial, there was genuine reasoning.

sentences.zh: 又為《毛詩義》，經籍疑滯，多所論釋。

translations.literal: He also wrote commentaries on the Mao Odes; doubtful points in the classics he largely discussed and explained.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote commentaries on the Mao Odes; doubtful points in the classics he largely discussed and explained.

sentences.zh: 嘗就沙門支僧納學，妙盡其能。

translations.literal: He once studied under the monk Zhi Sengna and fully mastered his abilities.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied under the monk Zhi Sengna and fully mastered his abilities.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王義宣自京口遷鎮江陵，要康之同行，距不應命。

translations.literal: Prince Yixuan of Jingling moved his post from Jingkou to Jiangling and wanted Kangzhi to go with him; he refused and did not respond to the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixuan of Jingling moved his post from Jingkou to Jiangling and wanted Kangzhi to go with him; he refused and did not respond to the summons.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，太祖聞康之有學義，除武昌國中軍將軍，蠲除租稅。

translations.literal: During Yuanjia, Emperor Taizu heard that Kangzhi had learning and principles; he appointed him Middle Army General of the Principality of Wuchang and exempted him from rent and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia, Emperor Taizu heard that Kangzhi had learning and principles; he appointed him Middle Army General of the Principality of Wuchang and exempted him from rent and taxes.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭、廣陵王誕臨南徐州，辟為從事、西曹，並不就。

translations.literal: Princes Jiangxia Yigong and Guangling Dan when administering South Xuzhou recruited him as Staff Member and Western Section Clerk; he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: When Princes Jiangxia Yigong and Guangling Dan administered South Xuzhou they recruited him as Staff Member and Western Section Clerk; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 棄絕人事，守志閒居。

translations.literal: He abandoned human affairs, guarded his will, and lived at leisure.
