translations.idiomatic: He abandoned human affairs, guarded his will, and lived at leisure.

sentences.zh: 弟雙之為臧質車騎參軍，與質俱下，至赭圻病卒，瘞於水濱。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shuang served as Staff Member to the Cavalry General Zang Zhi; going south with Zhi, he died of illness at Zheqi and was buried on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shuang served as Staff Member to the Cavalry General Zang Zhi; going south with Zhi, he died of illness at Zheqi and was buried on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 康之其春得疾困篤，小差，牽以迎喪，因得虛勞病，寢頓二十餘年。

translations.literal: That spring Kangzhi fell gravely ill; when slightly recovered he was pulled along to meet the funeral cortege and thereby contracted consumption; he lay prostrate for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Kangzhi fell gravely ill; when slightly recovered he was pulled along to meet the funeral cortege and thereby contracted consumption; he lay prostrate for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 時有閑日，輒臥論文義。

translations.literal: When he had leisure days he would lie down and discuss literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had a free day he would recline and discourse on literary and philosophical principles.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，遣大使陸子真巡行天下，使反，薦康之「業履恆貞，操勖清固，行信閭黨，譽延邦邑，棲志希古，操不可渝，宜加徵聘，以潔風軌。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne he sent Grand Envoy Lu Zizhen to tour the realm; when the envoy returned he recommended Kangzhi: "His conduct and footsteps are constantly steadfast, his discipline pure and firm, his conduct trusted in village and neighborhood, his fame extending through town and district; his dwelling will aspires to antiquity and his integrity cannot be altered—he should receive enhanced summons and appointment to purify custom and standards."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu took the throne he sent Grand Envoy Lu Zizhen to tour the realm; on his return the envoy recommended Kangzhi, writing that his conduct was steadfast, his integrity pure and firm, his reputation trusted in village and town, his aspirations turned toward antiquity and his resolve unshakable—he should be summoned to office to purify public morals.

sentences.zh: 不見省。

translations.literal: The recommendation was not acted upon.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始初，與平原明僧紹俱徵為通直郎，又辭以疾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, he and Ming Sengshao of Pingyuan were together summoned as Attendants in Direct Access; he again declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Taizong he and Ming Sengshao of Pingyuan were both summoned as Attendants in Direct Access; he again pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明元年，卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun he died, at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun he died, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫獨往之人，皆稟偏介之性，不能摧志屈道，借譽期通。

translations.literal: The historian says: Men who go their own way all receive a nature of partial integrity; they cannot break their will and bend the Way, borrowing reputation to await success.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Those who go their own way are all endowed with an uncompromising nature; they cannot bend their will or compromise the Way, nor trade on reputation in hope of advancement.

sentences.zh: 若使值見信之主，逢時來之運，豈其放情江海，取逸丘樊。

translations.literal: If they had met a lord who trusted them and encountered a timely coming fortune, how would they have released their feelings on rivers and seas and sought ease on hill and hedge!
translations.idiomatic: Had they met a ruler who truly trusted them and a timely age that called them forth, would they have poured their hearts into rivers and seas or sought ease only on hill and hedge?

sentences.zh: 蓋不得已而然故也。

translations.literal: It was because they had no choice but to be so.
translations.idiomatic: They acted thus because they had no alternative.

sentences.zh: 且巖壑閑遠，水石清華，雖復崇門八襲，高城萬雉，莫不蓄壤開泉，仿佛林澤。

translations.literal: Moreover, cliffs and ravines are tranquil and far, waters and stones pure and splendid—even though there are lofty gates eight layers deep and high walls with ten thousand battlements, none fail to store soil and open springs, resembling woods and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, cliffs and ravines are serene and remote, streams and stones pure and splendid—even mansions with gates eight layers deep and cities walled with ten thousand battlements all store earth and open springs, evoking woods and marshes.

sentences.zh: 故知松山桂渚，非止素玩，碧澗清潭，翻成麗矚。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that pine-covered mountains and cassia-lined islets are not merely plain diversions; jade-green streams and clear pools in turn become splendid sights.
translations.idiomatic: Thus pine-covered mountains and cassia-lined shores are not mere rustic pastimes; jade-green streams and clear pools become objects of refined delight.

sentences.zh: 掛冠東都，夫何難之有哉！

translations.literal: To hang up one's cap in the eastern capital—what difficulty is there in that!
translations.idiomatic: To hang up one's official cap and retire to the eastern capital—what could be easier than that!
